Quick Start Guide
As a player, you can use the League Management System to view your team schedules,
standings, match details, and club DUPR information.
If you belong to multiple teams, use the My Teams option in the sidebar to select which
team's dashboard and information you want to view.
Mobile Device Usage
The system is fully optimized for desktop computers, tablets, and mobile devices. Please
note that most of the screenshots and instructions in this guide are based on the desktop
version. Layouts, menus, and navigation will automatically adapt to your screen size, so
display and functionality may differ slightly when using a mobile device.
Understanding DUPR Ratings
Season DUPR ratings are displayed throughout the system. To learn how DUPR ratings are
calculated, visit this website: https://www.dupr.com/how-it-works. For questions about
how the Club uses DUPR ratings, which rating is used, or other DUPR-related topics, contact
info@lwrpickleballclub.com.

CAPTAIN/CO-CAPTAIN REQUIREMENTS
Each League team must have a designated Captain. A Captain may also serve as Co-Captain on
another team and may captain a team in the opposite gender category. However, a person may not
captain more than one team within the same gender category. There can be up to two Co-Captains.
Community Team Captains and Co-Captains have “Captain” access to the League Management
System (LMS) at league.lwrpickleballclub.com to manage teams, rosters, schedules, scores, and
overall league information. (For general club details, visit the main website at lwrpickleballclub.com).
Captains are responsible for their team roster, each match date setup including reserving all home
courts, recording/validating scores and general team management. Club League Management is
available at any time for help with any questions or concerns. See last page for contact information.
Team Home Court Expectations: All teams registering for league play are expected to host their share
of scheduled home matches by providing adequate court availability, resulting in a balanced home-
and-away schedule whenever possible. If a team cannot reserve enough courts for all its assigned
home match dates, additional matches may be scheduled as away games. Teams that are unable to
provide any courts due to limitations within their community or facility will play all their scheduled
matches as away games.
All league players also have access to the LMS through their personal Player Dashboard, where they
can view their assigned teams, upcoming and completed matches, team rosters, and standings. It also
features a full personal play history and quick-click shortcuts to email team captains. Captains can
also switch to the Player Dashboard to see their personal league information.

selected.content:
• Side Outs & Scoring: If the serving team loses a rally, a side out occurs; the
opposing team earns a point and takes over the serve.

• Scoring Freeze and Match Point: To keep the game competitive through the final
point, a scoring freeze shall take eƯect whenever a team reaches one point below
the game-winning score. Once a team reaches the freeze point, it may score the
game-winning point only while serving. For example, in a game played to 25 points,
a team’s score shall initially freeze at 24. The scoring freeze applies only to the team
that has reached the freeze point; the opposing team may continue to score using
normal Rally Scoring until it also reaches the applicable freeze point. A team must
be serving to score the game-winning point.

• Win-by-Two (2) Games: When the game is played using a win-by-two (2) format
and the score becomes tied at or beyond the initial freeze point, neither team can
win by scoring the next point. Therefore, both teams’ scores shall become
unfrozen, and normal Rally Scoring shall resume. Thereafter, a team’s score shall
freeze again whenever it reaches a score at which its next point would win the

PICKLEBREAKER™ GAME OVERVIEW
The Picklebreaker™ is our league’s tiebreaker format, similar to Major League Pickleball’s (MLP)
Dreambreaker. It is used when a match is tied after the day’s regular games. Unlike the MLP
version, our Picklebreaker uses doubles rather than singles.
Here is how it works:
The Format: The Picklebreaker™ is a doubles game played to either 15 or 25 points, depending
on the league. It always uses Rally Scoring, where every rally/serve earns a point regardless of
which team served. Refer to the league-specific rules for Rally Scoring, total points, and win-by
requirements.
The Rotations: Each team’s designated doubles pairs shall enter the game in the order
established by their captain prior to the start of play. Both doubles pairs currently on the
court shall remain in play until the combined game score reaches the next rotation
threshold, at which time both pairs shall rotate out and the next designated doubles pair from
each team shall enter.
For games played to 15 points, two (2) designated doubles pairs from each team shall
participate in the rotation, with substitutions occurring after every four (4) combined points
scored.
For games played to 25 points, six (6) designated doubles pairs from each team shall
participate in the rotation, with substitutions occurring after every four (4) combined points
scored.
Each newly substituted doubles pair shall resume play at the existing score and remain on the
court until the next applicable four (4) combined-point rotation threshold is reached.
If the game continues beyond the initial rotation of all designated doubles pairs, the
rotation shall return to the doubles pairs that began the game and continue in the same

Section 1 The Game
Pickleball is a paddle sport that combines elements of badminton, table
tennis, and tennis. It is played using a special perforated ball on a 20-foot
by 44-foot court with a tennis type net. The court is divided into right and
left service courts and a non-volley zone on each end of the net (Figure 3-1).
Pickleball can be played as singles or doubles.
In standard pickleball, the ball is served diagonally across the net to the
opposite service court on the opponent’s end, using an approved motion.
The ball is then hit back and forth across the net until a player fails to return
the ball in accordance with the rules.
Standard pickleball uses a scoring method where points are scored only
when the serving team wins the rally. The server alternates service courts
and continues to serve until they lose a rally (commit a fault). Typically, the
first player or team scoring 11 points and leading by at least a 2-point
margin wins the game.
Rally scoring has been provisionally approved as an option (Rule 14.A),
wherein a point is scored by the team that wins each rally. Mini-singles
(Rule 14.B) is a half-court variation of standard singles.

Two-Bounce Rule. After the serve, the receiver must allow the ball to
bounce before making their first return, and then the serving team must
allow the ball to bounce before making their first return.
Non-Volley Zone. The non-volley zone is the area of the court that
extends 7 feet from the net on each end of the court, within which a player
is not allowed to hit the ball out of the air before it bounces.
Wheelchair and Adaptive Play. Players using wheelchairs and players
having certain disabilities may allow the ball to bounce twice before
returning the ball. The first bounce must be in the court, but the second

point, a scoring freeze shall take eƯect whenever a team reaches one point below
the game-winning score. Once a team reaches the freeze point, it may score the
game-winning point only while serving. For example, in a game played to 25 points,

that has reached the freeze point; the opposing team may continue to score using

be serving to score the game-winning point.

player position or server error (see Rule 5.C.1.a), or to ask for
correction of an incorrect score before the return of serve (see Rule
6.F.1).

• Scoring Freeze and Match Point: To keep the game competitive through the final
point, a scoring freeze shall take eƯect whenever a team reaches one point below
the game-winning score. Once a team reaches the freeze point, it may score the
game-winning point only while serving. For example, in a game played to 25 points,
a team’s score shall initially freeze at 24. The scoring freeze applies only to the team
that has reached the freeze point; the opposing team may continue to score using
normal Rally Scoring until it also reaches the applicable freeze point. A team must
be serving to score the game-winning point.

• Win-by-Two (2) Games: When the game is played using a win-by-two (2) format
and the score becomes tied at or beyond the initial freeze point, neither team can
win by scoring the next point. Therefore, both teams’ scores shall become
unfrozen, and normal Rally Scoring shall resume. Thereafter, a team’s score shall
freeze again whenever it reaches a score at which its next point would win the

selected.content:
PICKLEBREAKER™ GAME OVERVIEW
The Picklebreaker™ is our league’s tiebreaker format, similar to Major League Pickleball’s (MLP)
Dreambreaker. It is used when a match is tied after the day’s regular games. Unlike the MLP
version, our Picklebreaker uses doubles rather than singles.
Here is how it works:
The Format: The Picklebreaker™ is a doubles game played to either 15 or 25 points, depending
on the league. It always uses Rally Scoring, where every rally/serve earns a point regardless of
which team served. Refer to the league-specific rules for Rally Scoring, total points, and win-by
requirements.
The Rotations: Each team’s designated doubles pairs shall enter the game in the order
established by their captain prior to the start of play. Both doubles pairs currently on the
court shall remain in play until the combined game score reaches the next rotation
threshold, at which time both pairs shall rotate out and the next designated doubles pair from
each team shall enter.
For games played to 15 points, two (2) designated doubles pairs from each team shall
participate in the rotation, with substitutions occurring after every four (4) combined points
scored.
For games played to 25 points, six (6) designated doubles pairs from each team shall
participate in the rotation, with substitutions occurring after every four (4) combined points
scored.
Each newly substituted doubles pair shall resume play at the existing score and remain on the
court until the next applicable four (4) combined-point rotation threshold is reached.
If the game continues beyond the initial rotation of all designated doubles pairs, the
rotation shall return to the doubles pairs that began the game and continue in the same

Section 1 The Game
Pickleball is a paddle sport that combines elements of badminton, table
tennis, and tennis. It is played using a special perforated ball on a 20-foot
by 44-foot court with a tennis type net. The court is divided into right and
left service courts and a non-volley zone on each end of the net (Figure 3-1).
Pickleball can be played as singles or doubles.
In standard pickleball, the ball is served diagonally across the net to the
opposite service court on the opponent’s end, using an approved motion.
The ball is then hit back and forth across the net until a player fails to return
the ball in accordance with the rules.
Standard pickleball uses a scoring method where points are scored only
when the serving team wins the rally. The server alternates service courts
and continues to serve until they lose a rally (commit a fault). Typically, the
first player or team scoring 11 points and leading by at least a 2-point
margin wins the game.
Rally scoring has been provisionally approved as an option (Rule 14.A),
wherein a point is scored by the team that wins each rally. Mini-singles
(Rule 14.B) is a half-court variation of standard singles.
Unique Features
Two-Bounce Rule. After the serve, the receiver must allow the ball to
bounce before making their first return, and then the serving team must
allow the ball to bounce before making their first return.
Non-Volley Zone. The non-volley zone is the area of the court that
extends 7 feet from the net on each end of the court, within which a player
is not allowed to hit the ball out of the air before it bounces.
Wheelchair and Adaptive Play. Players using wheelchairs and players
having certain disabilities may allow the ball to bounce twice before
returning the ball. The first bounce must be in the court, but the second

selected.content:
6.2. Saturday DUPR League
The Saturday DUPR League is designed for players who prefer weekend competition or are
unable to participate during the week. This coed league features community-based teams
made up of both men and women, competing every other Saturday in a unique format that
includes men's doubles, women's doubles, mixed doubles and the exciting mixed doubles
Picklebreaker to determine tied matches. Teams are grouped into divisions based on
combined DUPR ratings, creating competitive and enjoyable matches while fostering
camaraderie and community spirit throughout the Lakewood Ranch area.

Saturday DUPR League Match Day Format
The schedule uses two courts for men’s teams and two courts for women’s teams. After the first four
gender-doubles rounds, Men’s Team 3 and Women’s Team 6 play while Mixed Teams 7 and 8 begin.
Round 6 includes the remaining mixed teams. If the match is tied 12-12 after all gender and mixed
doubles, the Picklebreaker is played on two courts using the same mixed teams in the captains’
designated order.

Appendix B Rulebook Priorities and Guiding
Principles
Preface
The USA Pickleball Official Rulebook is the organization’s most important product.
It is the foundational document for the sport of pickleball and should be treated
with the respect accorded the sport’s founders and those who have written and
approved rules over the years.
Writing rules that are objective, clear, and concise is difficult work. Because those
involved in writing and/or approving rules come from diverse backgrounds and
experiences, it is important to have rule writing priorities and guiding principles
that help provide a measure of consistency from year to year. The following
Rulebook Priorities and Guiding Principles were developed to guide rule writers and
approvers in their important work.
Priorities

Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club
DUPR League Captains Guide
Welcome to the Captain & Co-Captain Guide! Think of this as your go-to manual for standard team
management and captain duties.
As a Captain or Co-Captain, we appreciate your commitment to both your community and your team
members. Your position is vital to the success of our League as well as to those you lead. We are here to
support you in fulfilling these responsibilities, and this guide has been prepared to oƯer comprehensive
answers and guidance to help facilitate your role as Captain/Co-Captain.

and match setup to score entry and standings tracking. For step-by-step technical instructions on
using the LMS, log in and click the Captains User Guide (question mark icon) in the top header.

6.2. Saturday DUPR League
The Saturday DUPR League is designed for players who prefer weekend competition or are
unable to participate during the week. This coed league features community-based teams
made up of both men and women, competing every other Saturday in a unique format that
includes men's doubles, women's doubles, mixed doubles and the exciting mixed doubles
Picklebreaker to determine tied matches. Teams are grouped into divisions based on
combined DUPR ratings, creating competitive and enjoyable matches while fostering
camaraderie and community spirit throughout the Lakewood Ranch area.

selected.content:
Saturday DUPR League Match Day Format
The schedule uses two courts for men’s teams and two courts for women’s teams. After the first four
gender-doubles rounds, Men’s Team 3 and Women’s Team 6 play while Mixed Teams 7 and 8 begin.
Round 6 includes the remaining mixed teams. If the match is tied 12-12 after all gender and mixed
doubles, the Picklebreaker is played on two courts using the same mixed teams in the captains’
designated order.

candidates.heading: LEAGUE FEES AND WAIVER
candidates.content:
LEAGUE FEES AND WAIVER
o The registration fee is per team, per division, per season, as announced before the season
begins. No refunds will be issued starting one week before the season starts, unless a division
is canceled due to having fewer than the four-team minimum or other league-initiated
cancelations.
o The League shall provide:
 Match Balls: Franklin Outdoor X-40 Optic balls for all regular season and playoƯ
matches.
 DUPR Uploads: All match results logged to DUPR for rating updates (excluding mixed
and individual Picklebreaker™ games and some tournament games).
 Administration: All scheduling, website management, and administrative support.
 Championship Prize: Free entry into the following season for the Gold Medal/1st place
team in each division based on Championship Day/PlayoƯ results.
o Waiver: As an LWR PC member, you acknowledge the risks of participation and release
LWR PC, match sites, communities/clubs, and all officers/volunteers from any claims,
liability, and costs. See the full detailed Waiver here: https://tinyurl.com/LWRPC-ClubWaiver

20.F Damaged Ball. A player may appeal to the referee to determine whether a
ball is degraded, soft, broken, or cracked. A potentially soft or degraded
ball will not be replaced unless all players agree. If the referee determines
that the ball is broken or cracked, it will be replaced. (Modifies Rule 10.G)

16.G Ball Selection. The Tournament Director will choose the tournament ball
from the official list of approved balls posted on the USA Pickleball website.

3.C Ball Specifications. The requirements for the ball are set forth in Rules 3.C.1
through 3.C.5. The complete list of approved balls is posted on the USA
Pickleball website.

directPassages:
24.B.1 Fault – Extra Ball Visible or Ball Falls. When an extra ball
carried by a player is visible to an opponent or falls to the
playing surface while the ball is live, it is a fault against the
player.

10.C Returned Ball Placement. A player must return the ball so that the ball
lands on the opponent’s end of the court or contacts the opponent or
anything that is worn or carried by the opponent before the ball lands.

13.I.2 Ball Crosses Back to Opponent’s Side. When a ball bounces in the
court on the receiving player’s end of the net and then returns to
the opponent’s side of the net without being hit, the receiving
player may cross over, under, or around the net to hit the ball, but
only after the ball has first crossed back to the opponent’s end of
the net.

7.B.2 No Manipulation or Spin Upon Release. Some natural rotation of
the ball is expected during any release of the ball. The server must
not manipulate the ball to add spin with any part of the server's
body or the paddle prior to hitting the ball to make the serve,
except that the server may allow the ball to roll off the face of the
paddle by gravity. Spin may be applied to the ball upon contact by
the paddle.

genericPassages:
17.D.14 Damaged Balls. Determine whether a ball is broken or cracked
and must be replaced, and whether the broken or cracked ball
affected the outcome of a rally. (See Rule 20.F.)
directPassages:
17.D.14 Damaged Balls. Determine whether a ball is broken or cracked
and must be replaced, and whether the broken or cracked ball
affected the outcome of a rally. (See Rule 20.F.)

13.I.1 After Hitting the Ball. A player may cross the plane of the net
immediately after hitting the ball. The allowance to cross the plane
of the net only applies while executing the current strike of the ball
and for continuation associated with the current strike of the ball.

10.G Damaged Ball. When a ball is or becomes broken, cracked, soft or degraded,
play must continue until the end of the rally. The ball will be replaced if all
players agree.

13.B Ball Contacting Net Support System. A served ball must not contact any
part of the net support system. A returned ball must not contact any part of
the net support system on the hitting player’s end of the net.

13.F Ball Crossing Plane of Net. A ball must entirely cross to a player’s end of
the net before the player hits the ball.

7.C.3 Ball Height. The ball must clearly be no higher than the server’s
waist when the paddle contacts the ball.

20.F.1 Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball. When the referee determines
that the broken or cracked ball affected the outcome of the rally,
the rally must be replayed with a replacement ball. (Modifies
Rule 10.G.1)

10.G.1 Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball. When all players agree that a
broken or cracked ball affected the outcome of the rally, the rally
must be replayed. If all players do not agree that a broken or
cracked ball affected the outcome of the rally, the result of the rally
stands.

13.B.2 Replay – Ball Affected by Net Support System. When a returned
ball crosses the net and contacts any part of a crossbar, or any
other part of the net support system within the court boundaries,
before or after the ball bounces, the rally must be replayed.

10.C.5 Fault – Ball Hits Permanent Object After Landing. When a player
fails to return a ball that has bounced in the player’s court before
the ball contacts a permanent object, it is a fault against that
player.

13.I.2.b Fault – Ball Not Contacted. When a ball bounces in
the court on the receiving player’s end of the net and
then returns to the opponent’s end of the net without
being hit, it is a fault against a player who fails to hit
the ball before it bounces once on the opponent’s end
of the net.

13.B.1 Fault – Ball Contacts Net Support System. When a player serves a
ball that contacts the net support system on either end of the net
or returns a ball that contacts the net support system before going
over the net, it is a fault against the player.

genericPassages:
3.C.1 Usage. All approved balls are acceptable for indoor or outdoor
play. (See Figure 3-2.)

directPassages:
20.E.2.a Replay – Ball Release Not Visible. When it is
questionable whether the release of the ball was not
visible to the referee and receiver, the referee may
call for a replay. When the referee is certain that the
release of the ball was not visible, the referee must
call for a replay.

24.B Extra Ball. An extra ball carried by a player during a rally must not be
visible to the opponent and must remain in possession of the player.

13.F.1 Fault – Ball Hit Before Crossing Plane of Net. When a player hits
the ball before the ball entirely crosses the plane of the net to the
player’s end, it is a fault against the player.

20.E.2.i Replay – Drop Serve, Questionable Force on Ball.
When it is questionable whether the ball was
propelled when the server released the ball to make
a drop serve, the referee must call for a replay.

7.B Ball Release. The server must comply with Rules 7.B.1 through 7.B.3 when
releasing the ball to make the serve.

selected.content:
6.1. Weekday DUPR League
The Weekday DUPR League is designed for players who have the flexibility to play during
the week and want a structured, team-based competitive experience. Men's and women's
divisions compete separately, with matches typically held at noon during the week. Teams
represent their home communities and travel throughout the Lakewood Ranch area to
compete against other community teams in a round-robin match format. Divisions are
organized using DUPR team rating ranges to promote balanced competition while providing
players with regular opportunities to improve their skills, build friendships, and enjoy the
excitement of representing their community.

26a0a36b-fdb3-46fc-94d5-360ea46d674b.heading: Saturday DUPR League Match Day Format
26a0a36b-fdb3-46fc-94d5-360ea46d674b.section: Saturday DUPR League Match Day Format
26a0a36b-fdb3-46fc-94d5-360ea46d674b.content:
Saturday DUPR League Match Day Format
The schedule uses two courts for men’s teams and two courts for women’s teams. After the first four
gender-doubles rounds, Men’s Team 3 and Women’s Team 6 play while Mixed Teams 7 and 8 begin.
Round 6 includes the remaining mixed teams. If the match is tied 12-12 after all gender and mixed
doubles, the Picklebreaker is played on two courts using the same mixed teams in the captains’
designated order.

3761e243-f5e8-43a8-bd9d-1a4cad6e211c.title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
3761e243-f5e8-43a8-bd9d-1a4cad6e211c.heading: Player Cap
3761e243-f5e8-43a8-bd9d-1a4cad6e211c.content:
6.2.5. Player Cap: Every player plays 3 gender double games to 15 and will then play 1
mixed game to 15. Optional lineups may include players who compete only in
gender doubles or only in mixed doubles. Depending on the outcome, the 6 mixed
teams will then play the Picklebreaker sequence playing up to 4+ points per team.

35b84937-eadb-4e4f-9f1d-cd05555769d4.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
35b84937-eadb-4e4f-9f1d-cd05555769d4.heading: 15.B Event Formats — Team Play
35b84937-eadb-4e4f-9f1d-cd05555769d4.content:
15.B.7 Team Play. Team play participants are designated by roster and
play can include gender singles, gender doubles, and mixed
doubles. Team play may use standard scoring or rally scoring for
both singles and doubles play.

c4d96411-9d9e-4ab6-9079-089e4d272fb9.title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
c4d96411-9d9e-4ab6-9079-089e4d272fb9.content:
6.2. Saturday DUPR League
The Saturday DUPR League is designed for players who prefer weekend competition or are
unable to participate during the week. This coed league features community-based teams
made up of both men and women, competing every other Saturday in a unique format that
includes men's doubles, women's doubles, mixed doubles and the exciting mixed doubles
Picklebreaker to determine tied matches. Teams are grouped into divisions based on
combined DUPR ratings, creating competitive and enjoyable matches while fostering
camaraderie and community spirit throughout the Lakewood Ranch area.

15.A.3 Doubles. A doubles team must consist of two players who meet
the classification requirements to participate in a particular
division of play.

7387f5a4-bedb-4567-8385-86196ecbbb87.title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
7387f5a4-bedb-4567-8385-86196ecbbb87.heading: Scoring
7387f5a4-bedb-4567-8385-86196ecbbb87.content:
6.2.4. Scoring: A maximum of 27 total possible match points per date. This includes 24
possible points awarded during standard play, plus a 3-point bonus. If the match
ends in a tie after the mixed doubles division (12-12), a Picklebreaker will be played
to determine the winner of the 3 bonus points. If there is no tie, the leading team
automatically receives the 3-point bonus.

2c9ed553-c425-43f0-b2e1-deadcda18cc3.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
2c9ed553-c425-43f0-b2e1-deadcda18cc3.heading: Partner Change (Doubles)
2c9ed553-c425-43f0-b2e1-deadcda18cc3.content:
18.G Partner Change (Doubles). With the Tournament Director’s approval, a
player may change a partner before a first-round match when the change is
due to injury, illness, or circumstances beyond the control of the player. A
partner change after the partners start team play is prohibited.

who uses a wheelchair, except as provided for in Rule 25.A.12 for
tournaments.

69ae6cdf-e0a5-457a-abce-9c69c15128e5.content:
1. CLUB LEAGUE FORMAT
1.1. Club main website: https://lwrpickleballclub.com
1.2. League Management System (LMS) website: https://league.lwrpickleballclub.com
1.3. There are three seasons: Fall, Winter, and Spring.
1.4. Each season consists of a multi-week regular play followed by championships/playoƯs.
1.5. League teams are divided by Divisions based on DUPR ratings.
1.6. The Leagues consist of:

a6be18a3-08fd-442d-8e29-ebcbbdd1e808.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
a6be18a3-08fd-442d-8e29-ebcbbdd1e808.heading: 15.A.3 Doubles — Age-Qualified Doubles Events
a6be18a3-08fd-442d-8e29-ebcbbdd1e808.content:
15.A.3.c Age-Qualified Doubles Events. In a doubles event
qualified by ages 19 years and older (adult event), the
age of the younger team member determines a team’s
age classification for the event. Players may play in a
younger age adult event unless prohibited by the rules
of the National Senior Games Association.

514699fc-e334-4821-a0da-0041bb76856a.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
514699fc-e334-4821-a0da-0041bb76856a.heading: 15.A.3 Doubles — Skill-Rated Doubles Events
514699fc-e334-4821-a0da-0041bb76856a.content:
15.A.3.b Skill-Rated Doubles Events. In a doubles event based
on player skill rating, the skill level of the higher-rated
team member determines a team’s skill rating for the
event.

8e938dc7-9e1d-43d5-bf1a-dc04aff10c6c.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
8e938dc7-9e1d-43d5-bf1a-dc04aff10c6c.heading: 15.B Event Formats — Double Elimination
8e938dc7-9e1d-43d5-bf1a-dc04aff10c6c.content:
15.B.1 Double Elimination. In a double elimination format, after losing
one match, a singles player or doubles team plays in a consolation
bracket. The player or team is eliminated from competition after
one loss in the consolation bracket. The winner of the consolation
bracket plays the winner of the winners’ bracket to determine first
place and second place. If the winner of the consolation bracket
defeats the winner of the winners’ bracket, then a tie-breaker
match to 15 points must be played to determine first place and
second place. The loser of the final match in the consolation
bracket wins third place.

Doubles. These team numbers correspond directly to the Match Score Sheet printed from the system.
We highly recommend assigning higher team numbers to teams with higher combined skill levels and
ratings (for instance, Team 6 should have a higher combined DUPR rating than Team 4 in Women’s or
Team 12 should be a higher team rating than Team 7 in Mixed Doubles).

4984124d-83a6-4671-a93e-8e12c0f33cc7.heading: 15.B Event Formats — Single Elimination with Consolation
4984124d-83a6-4671-a93e-8e12c0f33cc7.content:
15.B.2 Single Elimination with Consolation. In a single elimination with
consolation format, after losing one match, a singles player or
doubles team plays in a consolation bracket. The player or team is
eliminated from competition after one loss in the consolation
bracket. The final two players or teams in the winners’ bracket play
for first place and second place. The final two singles players or
doubles teams in the consolation bracket play for third place.

b36eec54-01f8-4a51-b9c7-77b5be74eba0.content:

may designate hybrid brackets or include hybrid pairings in

Appendix B Rulebook Priorities and Guiding
Principles
Preface
The USA Pickleball Official Rulebook is the organization’s most important product.
It is the foundational document for the sport of pickleball and should be treated
with the respect accorded the sport’s founders and those who have written and
approved rules over the years.
Writing rules that are objective, clear, and concise is difficult work. Because those
involved in writing and/or approving rules come from diverse backgrounds and
experiences, it is important to have rule writing priorities and guiding principles
that help provide a measure of consistency from year to year. The following
Rulebook Priorities and Guiding Principles were developed to guide rule writers and
approvers in their important work.
Priorities
The following three priorities should be considered “tests” for any suggested rule
change. Any suggested rule change should satisfy at least one of these three
priorities, listed in order of importance:
1. The first priority is preserving the integrity of the sport, one that incorporates
the elements of fun, cooperation, courtesy, and competition. This priority pays
homage to those who developed the sport in 1965 and those who have written
and approved rule changes over the years.
2. The second priority is what is collectively best for the players. This priority
examines rule changes for improving the player’s experience. It “tests”
suggested rule changes from the standpoint of minimizing player
disagreements, making it easier to learn the sport, teach the sport, and play
the sport, while also allowing for moderate innovation as player skills and
equipment develop and evolve.
3. The third priority is what is best for officiating. It “tests” rule changes to make it
less likely conflicts will occur between players as well as between players and
officials.
Guiding Principles
The USA Pickleball Official Rulebook contains a wide variety of rules that cover the
court and equipment, recreational and social play as well as tournament play,
officiated and non-officiated. The following are Guiding Principles for those writing
and approving rules. To the extent possible, rules should:
1. Apply to all levels and categories of players: recreational and social players, as
well as professional and amateur tournament players (officiated and non-
officiated). Specific rules for a single category of player, for example, the pro
level player, should be approved after careful consideration and examination
of how the rule change might impact the sport beyond the pro level of
competition.
2. Be written with a deterministic focus, i.e., from the standpoint of “if this occurs,
this is what happens.” If something is not allowed or should not happen, the
consequences (for example: replay, fault, technical warning, etc.) should be
provided as part of the rule (e.g., replay, fault, technical warning, etc.).
3. Center on that which should not occur, not on what is permitted or allowed.
Attempts to include rules describing what is allowed will result in an
unnecessarily lengthy Rulebook.
4. Avoid ambiguity, player discretion, or referee judgment-related rules. Such
rules invite disagreements and different interpretations. To this end, when a
key word is used to describe when a rule applies, the word should be defined
as either a part of the rule or in the Definition section of the Rulebook.
5. Allow equipment manufacturers to innovate, as long as such innovation does
not overwhelm or outpace the average player’s ability to keep up with the
speed and difficulty of the sport. Equipment-related rule changes should be
given particularly close scrutiny because of their precedent-setting potential.
6. Have an element of precedent accorded to them. Change for change’s sake
should be avoided to avoid frustration among, or a loss of confidence by,
players.
7. Allow for an appropriate degree of player innovation. Such innovation should
maintain a healthy balance between historical rules that have been
instrumental to the sport’s growth and appeal.
8. Preserve the unique features and rules of the sport involving the Non-Volley
Zone and the two-bounce rule and prevent one shot, one paddle, or one type
of play from dominating the sport.
9. Address a known issue or anticipate trends and needs of the sport before
problems develop.
10. Be subjected to reviews and comments by domestic and international
stakeholders.

dcd855f2-3d0f-4588-9281-99d260868035.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
dcd855f2-3d0f-4588-9281-99d260868035.heading: The Game
dcd855f2-3d0f-4588-9281-99d260868035.content:

Underlying Principles
Pickleball is a game that requires cooperation and courtesy. A sense of fair
play by giving the opponent the benefit of any doubt is essential in
maintaining the game’s underlying principles of fun and competition.
• All points played are treated the same regardless of their importance: the
first point of the match is as important as match point.
• Either partner in doubles can make calls, especially line calls.
• Calls are made promptly to preserve fair play and prevent players from
making delayed calls for their own advantage.
• Players strive to cooperate when confronted with a situation not covered
by the Rulebook. Resolutions can be made by asking for a referee to
resolve a dispute. allowing the rally to stand, or in extreme cases, a replay
of the rally.
• Where possible, rules accommodate players with various adaptive needs.
• Players avoid wearing clothing that closely matches the ball color.
• Players should not question or comment on an opponent’s call except
through an appeal to a referee.

5.B Doubles. Both players on a team will serve before a side out is declared,
except at the start of each game when only the starting server will serve as a

4b27a85a-c2d5-46c2-966b-3d113493f186.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
4b27a85a-c2d5-46c2-966b-3d113493f186.heading: 6.B Calling the Score — Doubles
4b27a85a-c2d5-46c2-966b-3d113493f186.section: Section 6: Player Readiness and Calling the
4b27a85a-c2d5-46c2-966b-3d113493f186.content:
6.B.2 Doubles. For doubles play, the score must be called as three
numbers: serving team’s score, then receiving team’s score, then
the server number. To start each game, the score will be called as
“zero – zero – two.”

01a0d25b-8753-4513-b4de-c58365aad0c1.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
01a0d25b-8753-4513-b4de-c58365aad0c1.heading: 6.B Calling the Score — Singles

01a0d25b-8753-4513-b4de-c58365aad0c1.content:
6.B.1 Singles. For singles play, the score must be called as two numbers:
server’s score, then receiver’s score. To start each game, the score
will be called as “zero – zero.”

27df8edb-72ab-405d-b933-1096ea7967b2.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
27df8edb-72ab-405d-b933-1096ea7967b2.heading: 5.B Doubles — Player Positions During Rallies
27df8edb-72ab-405d-b933-1096ea7967b2.content:
5.B.4 Player Positions During Rallies. Except while serving and
receiving, there is no restriction on the position of the players, on
or off the court, as long as they are on their respective end of the
net while the ball is live, except when a player crosses the plane of
the net as allowed in Rule 13.I.

9fdc27a4-e8ee-4eee-aa54-ea73c413f86d.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
9fdc27a4-e8ee-4eee-aa54-ea73c413f86d.heading: 15.B Event Formats — Single Elimination Without Consolation. (Pro and Senior Pro
9fdc27a4-e8ee-4eee-aa54-ea73c413f86d.content:
15.B.3 Single Elimination Without Consolation. (Pro and Senior Pro
Player Brackets) Single Elimination Without Consolation. The first
player/team to score the match-winning point by at least a two-
point margin wins. The final two players/teams in the winner’s
bracket play for the gold/first place and silver/second-place
medals. The determination of the final standings of the remaining
players/teams is left to the discretion of tournament officials.

e4bebbb3-7a89-42c6-ab33-dfb18baad0c3.title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules

c88f7dd2-f939-4ee9-93e9-fb0cc640606b.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
c88f7dd2-f939-4ee9-93e9-fb0cc640606b.heading: 6.B.2 Doubles — Score Call by Partner (Doubles)
c88f7dd2-f939-4ee9-93e9-fb0cc640606b.section: Section 6: Player Readiness and Calling the
c88f7dd2-f939-4ee9-93e9-fb0cc640606b.content:
6.B.2.a Score Call by Partner (Doubles). When a server is
unable to call the score, the server’s partner may call
the score. The same player must call the score
throughout the entire game unless the player’s voice
becomes impaired.

b5855fa3-bcf2-4c9a-952e-cdf4d3322f7f.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
b5855fa3-bcf2-4c9a-952e-cdf4d3322f7f.heading: 14.A (Provisional Rule) Rally Scoring Option — Serving (Doubles)
b5855fa3-bcf2-4c9a-952e-cdf4d3322f7f.content:
14.A.4 Serving (Doubles). After each side out, service begins with the
player correctly positioned on the right side according to the
team’s score. The server will alternate serving areas after each
point is won, until a rally is lost . (Modifies Rule 5.B.2)

0961effe-bfc3-4d78-9ad5-ccdb0bef86d8.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
0961effe-bfc3-4d78-9ad5-ccdb0bef86d8.heading: 14.A (Provisional Rule) Rally Scoring Option — One Server (Doubles)
0961effe-bfc3-4d78-9ad5-ccdb0bef86d8.content:
14.A.5 One Server (Doubles). Only one player on a team will serve before
a side out is declared. After the serving team loses the rally, a side
out will occur, and service is awarded to the opponent. (Modifies
Rules 5.B, 5.B.2, 5.B.5, 5.B.6)

57804f58-1392-4d41-af5e-12beeb29681c.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
57804f58-1392-4d41-af5e-12beeb29681c.heading: 10.D Double Hit — Fault – Ball Hit by Two-Players
57804f58-1392-4d41-af5e-12beeb29681c.content:
10.D.2 Fault – Ball Hit by Two-Players. It is a fault if both a player and
their partner strike the ball while attempting to return it.

f9394ad5-328d-4da7-a9a8-29fc26e48a83.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
f9394ad5-328d-4da7-a9a8-29fc26e48a83.heading: 15.A Event Categories. — Gender Events
f9394ad5-328d-4da7-a9a8-29fc26e48a83.content:
15.A.1 Gender Events. In events categorized by gender, only members of
that gender are allowed to play in that event.

2070049f-fd52-4006-b824-8ce27ea67758.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
2070049f-fd52-4006-b824-8ce27ea67758.heading: 15.A Event Categories. — Open Gender and Age Events
2070049f-fd52-4006-b824-8ce27ea67758.content:
15.A.2 Open Gender and Age Events. Players of any gender and age are
allowed to play in an open gender and age event.

e9995c8f-fc14-4fe7-87be-a33965861246.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
e9995c8f-fc14-4fe7-87be-a33965861246.heading: 5.B Doubles — Correct Serving and Receiving Positions
e9995c8f-fc14-4fe7-87be-a33965861246.content:
5.B.3 Correct Serving and Receiving Positions. The correct positions of
the server and receiver for each rally are determined by their
team’s score. When serving or receiving, the starting server's
correct position is on the right side of the court when their team’s
score is zero or even, and on the left side of the court when their
score is odd. When serving or receiving, the starting server’s
partner's correct position is on the left side of the court when their
team’s score is zero or even and on the right side of the court when
their score is odd.

9d4c194b-9743-4465-bcd9-5d67d82eba8d.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
9d4c194b-9743-4465-bcd9-5d67d82eba8d.heading: Double Hit
9d4c194b-9743-4465-bcd9-5d67d82eba8d.content:
10.D Double Hit. Balls can be hit more than once, but the stroke must be
continuous in a single direction by one player.

a2c1c86e-802f-4d3b-9dd8-67b8548456fd.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
a2c1c86e-802f-4d3b-9dd8-67b8548456fd.heading: 15.B Event Formats — Non-Pool Play
a2c1c86e-802f-4d3b-9dd8-67b8548456fd.content:
15.B.6 Non-Pool Play. After playing a round robin to determine seeding,
seeded singles players or doubles teams play a single-elimination
or double-elimination playoff, using a match format of two of three
games to 11 points, one game to 15 points, or one game to 21
points, all win by two points.

7fd765f3-3f03-4fe1-9e4e-2774e6ba4910.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
7fd765f3-3f03-4fe1-9e4e-2774e6ba4910.heading: 23.A Retirement from Match — Eligibility to Continue Play
7fd765f3-3f03-4fe1-9e4e-2774e6ba4910.content:
23.A.3 Eligibility to Continue Play. A singles player or doubles team
that retires from a match may continue play in the same bracket
if eligible based on the event format.

855fed46-6fd5-46cd-8e5a-500ff917e7d4.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
855fed46-6fd5-46cd-8e5a-500ff917e7d4.heading: 15.B Event Formats — Round Robin
855fed46-6fd5-46cd-8e5a-500ff917e7d4.content:
15.B.4 Round Robin. All singles players or doubles teams play each other.
The winner is determined based on the highest number of matches
won. When two or more teams are tied for the number of matches
won, ties must be broken in accordance with the sequence in Rules
15.B.4.a through 15.B.4.f. The method that succeeds in breaking
the tie will be used to rank all tied teams.

f4485503-ceb5-4ecf-9d40-15abd1befa9b.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
f4485503-ceb5-4ecf-9d40-15abd1befa9b.heading: 15.B Event Formats — Pool Play
f4485503-ceb5-4ecf-9d40-15abd1befa9b.content:
15.B.5 Pool Play. The singles players or doubles teams are divided into
two or more player pools. Each pool plays a round robin to seed
the players or teams for a single-elimination or double-elimination
playoff.

b5a8250d-5e2d-42e2-bca4-1f8e6d6a5e1e.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
b5a8250d-5e2d-42e2-bca4-1f8e6d6a5e1e.heading: Part IV: Rules for Inclusive Play
b5a8250d-5e2d-42e2-bca4-1f8e6d6a5e1e.section: Part IV: Rules for Inclusive Play
b5a8250d-5e2d-42e2-bca4-1f8e6d6a5e1e.content: Part IV Rules for Inclusive Play

37b9a4a2-954e-4a43-9b26-14047e8e25ca.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
37b9a4a2-954e-4a43-9b26-14047e8e25ca.heading: 25.B Adaptive Standing Play — Tournament Events
37b9a4a2-954e-4a43-9b26-14047e8e25ca.content:
25.B.4 Tournament Events. Adaptive standing players may play in any
event that allows standing players with either standing players
or partners, or wheelchair players or partners. Only adaptive
standing players are allowed to play in adaptive standing-only
events. Adaptive standing players may play in hybrid events. In
all cases, the specific rules governing adaptive standing players
apply to any player who is eligible, regardless of the event
format or the classification of their opponents or partners.

b8a2213f-32e7-48cf-9c3c-41fb9c28815b.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
b8a2213f-32e7-48cf-9c3c-41fb9c28815b.heading: 15.B.4 Round Robin — Withdrawal, Retirement, or Forfeit
b8a2213f-32e7-48cf-9c3c-41fb9c28815b.content:
15.B.4.a Withdrawal, Retirement, or Forfeit. When a singles
player or doubles team withdraws, retires, or is
forfeited from a round robin event, then that player’s
or team’s match results will not count toward the
standings of that event and the player or team will not
be eligible to participate in any elimination playoff or
medal match for that event. The match results will
count towards the player’s or team’s rating.

76da7fcb-5ee1-4407-be00-cd67614b9958.heading: 23.B Withdrawal from Bracket — Ineligibility to Continue Play
76da7fcb-5ee1-4407-be00-cd67614b9958.content:
23.B.3 Ineligibility to Continue Play. A singles player or doubles team

5545579f-0251-4b3f-aed9-a3091730304b.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
5545579f-0251-4b3f-aed9-a3091730304b.heading: 25.A Wheelchair Play — Tournament Events
5545579f-0251-4b3f-aed9-a3091730304b.content:
25.A.12 Tournament Events. Wheelchair players may compete in any
tournament event, other than an adaptive standing-only
event, and may partner with or compete against either
standing players, adaptive standing players, or wheelchair
players. Only wheelchair players are allowed to play in
wheelchair-only events. In all cases, the specific rules
governing wheelchair players apply to any player who uses a
wheelchair, regardless of the event format or the classification
of their opponents or partners.

7c3e358d-cce7-476d-a134-535c49296c9e.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
7c3e358d-cce7-476d-a134-535c49296c9e.heading: 14.B.1 The Court — Court Area In Play
7c3e358d-cce7-476d-a134-535c49296c9e.content:
14.B.1.a Court Area In Play. Only the right or left side on each
player’s end of the court is in play during each rally
based on each player’s respective score. (Modifies
Rules 3.A.4.c, 5.A.1)

0a746ff2-b9e4-4a07-8dfc-17ac6c0b8997.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
0a746ff2-b9e4-4a07-8dfc-17ac6c0b8997.heading: 15.B.4 Round Robin — Second Tie-Breaker
0a746ff2-b9e4-4a07-8dfc-17ac6c0b8997.content:
15.B.4.c Second Tie-Breaker. The second tie-breaker is the
best point differential of all games played. This tie-
breaker does not apply across multiple pools where
the number of teams in each pool is not equal. (For
example, Team A wins their first match, 11-8, 11-4, so
they would have a point differential of +10. Team A
then wins the second match, 11-9, 2-11, 11-6. For the
second round, they would have a point differential of -
2. This would give them a total for the two rounds of
+8.)

cee21b68-72fe-443f-a151-1f2b7644055d.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
cee21b68-72fe-443f-a151-1f2b7644055d.heading: 15.B.4 Round Robin — Fourth Tie-Breaker
cee21b68-72fe-443f-a151-1f2b7644055d.content:
15.B.4.e Fourth Tie-Breaker. The fourth tie-breaker is the best
point differential of games played against the singles
player or doubles team with the next -highest number
of matches won. (For example, when players or teams
are tied for second-place, the total point differential
against the first-place singles player or doubles team is
used.)

5cd80673-544a-4f0a-b474-26d13f18ef2b.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook

c524d6d2-34d8-41ed-8fd6-40cf4c5e0e09.content:

o Enter or update your player team roster prior to the commencement of each season. Use the

join, they can visit: https://lwrpickleballclub.com/signup.

https://www.dupr.com.

separate from the LWR PC membership) so we can accurately sync player ratings.
Captains should share this link with all players: https://tinyurl.com/LWRPC-DUPRCLUB.
o Roster Requirements & Substitutes: Teams must roster enough players and substitutes (who
are not already on another team) to field a full lineup weekly. For example, if your match
requires 6 players, an 8–10 player roster is recommended. Additional substitutes may be drawn
from other teams in the same community, provided they meet the DUPR division rating
requirements. For complete details, see the Player Requirements and DUPR Rating/Divisions
sections in the DUPR League Mission and Rules.
o Captain Roster Control: Captains are responsible for building their own rosters and may add
or delete players throughout the season as needed provided the player is a current, valid
member of the LWR PC, has a DUPR ID and is eligible for that division.
o Player DUPR Ratings: Season DUPR ratings are updated in the LMS before the season starts
and remain visible to captains all season. For players added midseason, their rating is based on

5.13.1. Less than half of the games completed: Remaining games should be

it must participate and maintain their original positions/line assignments.

5b432210-b886-44b6-a6e4-5b2312b07dee.title: LWRPC-Captains Guide to the LMS
5b432210-b886-44b6-a6e4-5b2312b07dee.content:
Match Setup Process
Captains must assign player pairings and save their lineups before the match date. To
ensure fair play, the system automatically checks entries against division ranges, team
totals, and Season DUPR ratings, displaying an on-screen warning if a combination is
ineligible. It is highly recommended that the Home Team enter their lineup first. Lineups
can be changed prior to match day with all changes automatically emailed to opposing
captains.
• In Match Setup, roster choices are filtered against the division’s configured rating
type: Season DUPR, or Age-based/PrimeTime (season_primetime_rating). Players
with no valid rating or outside the division minimum/maximum cannot be selected.
It also checks the two-player combined rating cap.
• Before saving, it refreshes the season ratings and validates again. The save API
repeats that validation server-side, including roster membership, individual rating
range, duplicates, and team-rating maximum.
The rating source is selected by the division’s rating_type: standard divisions use Season
DUPR; PrimeTime/Age-based divisions use the Season PrimeTime rating.
The Match Setup button will show as red if your setup is incomplete, and blue once it is
completed. When both teams have completed their setup, the Match Score Sheet button
will turn green, allowing you to print a complete match score sheet.
Saving a lineup (press the Save Match Setup button) automatically notifies the opposing
captain of the update. From this screen, you can also use the Email Players button to notify
all selected players or the entire team.
For any questions regarding player ratings or eligibility, contact
info@lwrpickleballclub.com.
Match Setup Window

6e572a43-4aed-47a8-89fc-518ecb52e7e9.content:
CAPTAINS NORMAL WEEKLY PROCESS
o Captain Match Duties: For every match, captains or co-captains must set their lineup (Match
Setup), print the score sheet, and enter or validate final scores.

before match day. It is recommended that the Home Team enter their lineups first.
 Updates: You can modify your lineup until match day. The system automatically emails
changes to the opposing captain.
 Penalties: Repeated incomplete or late lineup submissions may result in match
forfeiture, subject to League Management discretion.
o Match Day Team Responsibilities:
o The Home team is responsible for:
 Bringing league-provided balls.
 Printing the physical score sheet and recording match results.
 Entering final scores into the system after the match.
o The Visitor team is responsible for:
 Visiting captains may print a backup score sheet, but official score recording is the
home team's duty.

6199f5a5-c9a3-4706-bc06-d17faaf4a72e.title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR Captains Guide
6199f5a5-c9a3-4706-bc06-d17faaf4a72e.heading: CAPTAIN/CO-CAPTAIN REQUIREMENTS
6199f5a5-c9a3-4706-bc06-d17faaf4a72e.content:
CAPTAIN/CO-CAPTAIN REQUIREMENTS
Each League team must have a designated Captain. A Captain may also serve as Co-Captain on
another team and may captain a team in the opposite gender category. However, a person may not
captain more than one team within the same gender category. There can be up to two Co-Captains.
Community Team Captains and Co-Captains have “Captain” access to the League Management
System (LMS) at league.lwrpickleballclub.com to manage teams, rosters, schedules, scores, and
overall league information. (For general club details, visit the main website at lwrpickleballclub.com).
Captains are responsible for their team roster, each match date setup including reserving all home
courts, recording/validating scores and general team management. Club League Management is
available at any time for help with any questions or concerns. See last page for contact information.
Team Home Court Expectations: All teams registering for league play are expected to host their share
of scheduled home matches by providing adequate court availability, resulting in a balanced home-
and-away schedule whenever possible. If a team cannot reserve enough courts for all its assigned
home match dates, additional matches may be scheduled as away games. Teams that are unable to
provide any courts due to limitations within their community or facility will play all their scheduled
matches as away games.
All league players also have access to the LMS through their personal Player Dashboard, where they
can view their assigned teams, upcoming and completed matches, team rosters, and standings. It also
features a full personal play history and quick-click shortcuts to email team captains. Captains can
also switch to the Player Dashboard to see their personal league information.

through each non-volley zone. The color of the
additional line is not required to be the same as the
other court lines. (Modifies Rule 3.A.4.d)

68b8797b-2af0-46d5-a30d-49c967d58f0a.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
68b8797b-2af0-46d5-a30d-49c967d58f0a.heading: 3.A Court Specifications — Court Dimensions
68b8797b-2af0-46d5-a30d-49c967d58f0a.content:
3.A.1 Court Dimensions. The court must be a rectangle measuring 20
feet (6.10 m) wide and 44 feet (13.41 m) long for both singles and
doubles matches. (See Figure 3-1.)

5cf550f0-c000-479e-964d-bac741b7e020.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
5cf550f0-c000-479e-964d-bac741b7e020.heading: 17.B Pre-Match Checks — Court Conditions
5cf550f0-c000-479e-964d-bac741b7e020.content:
17.B.2 Court Conditions. Check the preparation of the court with respect
to cleanliness, lighting, net height, court markings, and hazards.

664e4268-dcc1-4ed3-8310-54e851db116e.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
664e4268-dcc1-4ed3-8310-54e851db116e.heading: 3.A.4 Lines and Areas — Service Courts
664e4268-dcc1-4ed3-8310-54e851db116e.content:
3.A.4.f Service Courts. The areas on each end of the court
between the non-volley zone and the baseline on
either side of the centerline. The right and left service
courts are bounded by and include their adjacent
baseline, sideline, and the centerline.

be478610-7cd2-4252-abd0-87c86906cef7.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
be478610-7cd2-4252-abd0-87c86906cef7.heading: Court Changes
be478610-7cd2-4252-abd0-87c86906cef7.content:
16.N Court Changes. The Tournament Director may direct a court change during
a match after the completion of any game to accommodate better spectator
or playing conditions.

aa1eec61-c551-49a2-8705-07c82de6205a.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
aa1eec61-c551-49a2-8705-07c82de6205a.heading: 3.A Court Specifications — Court Measurements
aa1eec61-c551-49a2-8705-07c82de6205a.content:
3.A.2 Court Measurements. Court measurements must be made to the
outside edge of the perimeter and non-volley zone lines.

5e85cc98-49b3-444d-ab13-16c50372878c.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
5e85cc98-49b3-444d-ab13-16c50372878c.heading: 7.A Server Positioning — Outside Court
5e85cc98-49b3-444d-ab13-16c50372878c.content:
7.A.2 Outside Court. Neither of the server’s feet is allowed to be in
contact with the court when the serve is hit.

4807a480-e196-4033-9fe8-43158453209d.title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
4807a480-e196-4033-9fe8-43158453209d.heading: Coaching & Court Access
4807a480-e196-4033-9fe8-43158453209d.content:
5.8. Coaching & Court Access: Coaching is permitted only during timeouts or between
games. Coaches and non-players must always remain oƯ the court; only active players
may be on the courts.
5.9. Spectator Interference: Spectators/non-participants must not be consulted on any call,
nor shall they influence any calls or decisions on the court.

1e2b76c8-a329-4de3-944f-943e3ec28125.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
1e2b76c8-a329-4de3-944f-943e3ec28125.heading: 7.A.2 Outside Court — Fault – Server Contacting Court
1e2b76c8-a329-4de3-944f-943e3ec28125.content:
7.A.2.a Fault – Server Contacting Court. If a server’s foot is in
contact with the court when the serve is hit, it is a fault
against the server.

d7236cbd-3e58-4413-ad27-b1de7a60c452.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
d7236cbd-3e58-4413-ad27-b1de7a60c452.heading: 3.A.4 Lines and Areas — Baselines
d7236cbd-3e58-4413-ad27-b1de7a60c452.content:
3.A.4.a Baselines. The lines parallel to the net at each end of
the court.

7f39cf32-b862-4792-a0d1-6d0e590a2e29.title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
7f39cf32-b862-4792-a0d1-6d0e590a2e29.heading: TEAM/GAME RULES
7f39cf32-b862-4792-a0d1-6d0e590a2e29.content:
5. TEAM/GAME RULES
5.1. Team Home Court Expectations: All teams registering for league play are expected to
host their share of scheduled home matches by providing adequate court availability,
resulting in a balanced home-and-away schedule whenever possible. If a team cannot
reserve enough courts for all its assigned home match dates, additional matches may be
scheduled as away games. Teams that are unable to provide any courts due to limitations
within their community or facility will play all their scheduled matches as away games.
5.2. Governing Rules & Equipment Standards: All matches are governed by USA Pickleball
Rules (https://usapickleball.org/) and equipment standards including USA Pickleball
approved equipment. In the event of a conflict, specific Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club
(LWR PC) rules shall take precedence over the corresponding USA Pickleball rules and
regulations.
5.3. Unauthorized Equipment Penalty: Games played with unauthorized paddles or
equipment will be forfeited, not recorded, and not posted to DUPR if discovered by
players/captains during or after play.

7f8f123b-8dab-4352-a153-e856d7917aef.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
7f8f123b-8dab-4352-a153-e856d7917aef.heading: 25.A.8 Serving — Fault – Wheel Contacting Court
7f8f123b-8dab-4352-a153-e856d7917aef.content:
25.A.8.b Fault – Wheel Contacting Court. If a large rear
wheel of a server’s wheelchair is in contact with the
court when the serve is hit, it is a fault against the
server. (Modifies Rule 7.A.2.a)

3745a0d6-26fa-4e28-a44b-67d08e2ea883.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
3745a0d6-26fa-4e28-a44b-67d08e2ea883.heading: 3.A Court Specifications — Lines and Areas
3745a0d6-26fa-4e28-a44b-67d08e2ea883.content:
3.A.4 Lines and Areas. The lines and areas of the standard pickleball
court are described in Rules 3.A.4.a through 3.A.4.g. (See Figure 3-
1.)

4f7eb9ed-cd6a-40e4-ab65-8f6f0e4b9ebe.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
4f7eb9ed-cd6a-40e4-ab65-8f6f0e4b9ebe.heading: Court Specifications
4f7eb9ed-cd6a-40e4-ab65-8f6f0e4b9ebe.content:
3.A Court Specifications. The dimensions and measurements for the standard
pickleball court are shown in Figure 3-1.
Figure 3-1: Court Specifications

922fe3da-3e22-4e00-9046-6976c3756287.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
922fe3da-3e22-4e00-9046-6976c3756287.heading: 3.A.4 Lines and Areas — Line Size and Color
922fe3da-3e22-4e00-9046-6976c3756287.content:
3.A.4.e Line Size and Color. All lines should be 2 inches (5.08
cm) wide and the same color, clearly contrasting with
the color of the playing surface and court.

53fe28c0-3492-4a7e-b71e-a3543ce98eb7.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
53fe28c0-3492-4a7e-b71e-a3543ce98eb7.heading: 3.A.4 Lines and Areas — Sidelines
53fe28c0-3492-4a7e-b71e-a3543ce98eb7.content:
3.A.4.b Sidelines. The two lines bounding the court that are
perpendicular to the net and baselines.

fda71efc-c8be-4f0b-b148-9626618f740a.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
fda71efc-c8be-4f0b-b148-9626618f740a.heading: 14.B.1 The Court — Boundary Lines
fda71efc-c8be-4f0b-b148-9626618f740a.content:
14.B.1.b Boundary Lines. The boundary lines of the in-play side
of the court for a rally are the baseline, the respective
sideline, and the centerline of the court. The opposite
side of the court is out of bounds.

d6e1f23c-fbe1-4434-a258-3a6558993f8d.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
d6e1f23c-fbe1-4434-a258-3a6558993f8d.heading: 3.A.4 Lines and Areas — Serving Areas
d6e1f23c-fbe1-4434-a258-3a6558993f8d.content:
3.A.4.g Serving Areas. The areas behind the baseline on each
end of the court. The right and left serving areas are
bounded by and include the imaginary extensions of
their adjacent sideline and the centerline.

6804ee96-3b70-486d-8554-927542297daa.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
6804ee96-3b70-486d-8554-927542297daa.heading: 3.A.4 Lines and Areas — Non-Volley Zone
6804ee96-3b70-486d-8554-927542297daa.content:
3.A.4.c Non-Volley Zone. The 7-foot by 20-foot (2.13.m by
6.08 m) area of the court adjacent to each end of the
net. The non-volley zone lines run parallel to the net, 7
feet (2.13 m) from the net on each end between the
two sidelines. All lines that bound the non-volley zone
are part of the zone. The non-volley zone is two-
dimensional and does not extend above the playing
surface.

3471f143-be00-42a9-9660-9b3b4917581c.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
3471f143-be00-42a9-9660-9b3b4917581c.heading: 3.A.4 Lines and Areas — Centerline
3471f143-be00-42a9-9660-9b3b4917581c.content:
3.A.4.d Centerline. The line down the center of the court on
each end of the court extending from the non-volley
zone line to the baseline. The centerline separates the
right and left service courts.

bce661ca-ab74-42d1-9086-d12a6b35e69d.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
bce661ca-ab74-42d1-9086-d12a6b35e69d.heading: 3.A Court Specifications — Playing Surface
bce661ca-ab74-42d1-9086-d12a6b35e69d.content:
3.A.3 Playing Surface. The minimum playing surface area is 30 feet
(9.14 m) wide and 60 feet (18.29 m) long. Other recommendations
for playing surface dimensions are:

(meters)

12137834-4d71-4c9e-baaf-e081c4c5aa89.content:
Quick Start Guide
As a player, you can use the League Management System to view your team schedules,
standings, match details, and club DUPR information.
If you belong to multiple teams, use the My Teams option in the sidebar to select which
team's dashboard and information you want to view.
Mobile Device Usage
The system is fully optimized for desktop computers, tablets, and mobile devices. Please
note that most of the screenshots and instructions in this guide are based on the desktop
version. Layouts, menus, and navigation will automatically adapt to your screen size, so
display and functionality may differ slightly when using a mobile device.
Understanding DUPR Ratings
Season DUPR ratings are displayed throughout the system. To learn how DUPR ratings are
calculated, visit this website: https://www.dupr.com/how-it-works. For questions about
how the Club uses DUPR ratings, which rating is used, or other DUPR-related topics, contact
info@lwrpickleballclub.com.

af393e89-06b0-406c-99ab-eaffeb369c7c.content:
Logging Into the System
The League Management System is located at https://league.lwrpickleballclub.com. Enter
your email address and password to sign in.
• First-Time Users: Enter the email address associated with your Club Membership
and click Forgot Password. A setup or a password reset email will be sent from no-
reply@auth.lwrpickleballclub.com to create your password. If you aren't sure which
email address you used, contact info@lwrpickleballclub.com.
• Passkeys & Biometrics: To log in using a passkey or fingerprint, click the Passkey
/ Fingerprint button to sign in or set up the feature.
Resetting Your Password
Select Forgot Password to reset or create your password. You can also change your
password at any time when you are logged in the system. Click the Change Password
button located in the top header of the initial dashboard screen. Note: this will only change
the password in this League Management System and not the Club Membership system.

HOW TO REGISTER YOUR TEAM (SIGNING UP YOUR TEAM)
• When registration opens for an upcoming league season, the Club will notify previous Captains and
other Club members that league registration is open.
• Visit the Club’s Leagues page at https://lwrpickleballclub.com/leagues and select the
appropriate league you wish to join.
• On the league registration page, begin the team registration process by clicking Register My Team!
• You must be signed into your regular Club membership account before you can register a team.
• Once you are signed into your Club membership account, select the Quantity and choose 1 to
register one team. If you need to register multiple teams, please complete the registration process
separately for each team.

d5cdf6d2-28a2-46fb-925f-1a84b50bcce8.heading: CLUB LEAGUE MANAGERS
d5cdf6d2-28a2-46fb-925f-1a84b50bcce8.content:
CLUB LEAGUE MANAGERS
Team captains should first attempt to resolve disputes directly, relying on common sense and fair play.
If they cannot reach an agreement, or if further issues arise during the season, Club League Managers
will review the matter. All decisions by Club League Managers are final and cannot be appealed.
For questions or concerns, please reach out to one of the following Club League Managers:
• Bill Weihs – Club League Co-Chair > bill@lwrpickleballclub.com
• Terry Adelman – Club League Co-Chair > terry@lwrpickleballclub.com

Player Dashboard Overview
The dashboard gives you quick access to your teams, upcoming matches, completed
matches, team standings, and your play history. If you are a member of multiple teams,
select the correct team under My Team in the sidebar to update the view.
Dashboard Highlights:
• Top Navigation: At the very top right of the Player Dashboard, you can access the
Player User Guide, email the league, or click the button next to your name to update
your profile, change your password, adjust appearance settings, or view your club
membership.
• Sidebar Options: Use the sidebar menu to switch between teams if you belong to
more than one, view your personal Play History, and check the Division Schedule
or Standings. Select League Documents to view all available files for your league.
• Team Information: The main dashboard gives you immediate access to your next
match, including buttons for match details and posted lineups. You can monitor your
team's rank, record, and your personal Season DUPR rating, as well as review
upcoming schedules and recent results.
• In the My Team section, click on any captain to send them an email, or select View
Team to see the complete player roster with DUPR ratings and individual records.

19a6da2c-4f5a-4d15-bef3-c75da9009d5a.content:
VIEW SCHEDULE/GAME INFORMATION
o On the Captain Dashboard, the selected team’s “next match” will be displayed along with
options for that match.
o Match Setup & Lineups: Captains must enter their lineups before match day to verify player
and team ratings. For complete details, see the Team/Game Rules in the DUPR League Rules.
o Completed Matches: Scroll down to the Recent results section to review score details for
past matches. Click on a match to see all detailed results including players and individual game
scores.
o Court Reservations & Match Details: The home team captain must reserve the required
number of courts for warm-ups and match play. You should confirm the start time and share all
location details with the visiting captain beforehand by clicking the Email Opposing Captains
button.
o Finding Captain Contact Info: Click the Division Captains button in the Captain Tools block
to view or print contact details for all captains and co-captains in your division.

managers by clicking the Contact League (email icon) button at the top of the screen.

match and record all scores on a printed Match Score Sheet. Keep these physical score sheets
on file for the remainder of the season.

6. LEAGUES
6.1. Weekday DUPR League
The Weekday DUPR League is designed for players who have the flexibility to play during
the week and want a structured, team-based competitive experience. Men's and women's
divisions compete separately, with matches typically held at noon during the week. Teams
represent their home communities and travel throughout the Lakewood Ranch area to
compete against other community teams in a round-robin match format. Divisions are
organized using DUPR team rating ranges to promote balanced competition while providing
players with regular opportunities to improve their skills, build friendships, and enjoy the
excitement of representing their community.

5.14. End of Season PlayoƯs/Championship Day (All Leagues)
5.14.1. Teams starting the season with fewer scheduled games than others in their
Division/Pool will receive compensatory points at the end of the season. These
points will be calculated based on the team’s average points earned per match
date, rounded to the nearest whole number (0.5 and above rounds up; 0.4 and
below rounds down).
5.14.2. PlayoƯs feature the top 4 teams per Division based on the LMS points; ties are
settled by Line/Game Win %, then point diƯerential, and finally a coin flip. For
divisions with 2 pools, the top 2 teams from each pool advance to playoƯs.
5.14.3. PlayoƯs will take place the week following the last regular season games, with all
games played at one location.
5.14.4. Captains will form teams following regular season rules and Season DUPR ratings.
5.14.5. Players may participate in a Division end-of-season/Championship game only if
they have competed in at least one game within that Division during the current
regular season.
5.14.6. A round-robin format will be implemented instead of traditional matchups: players
in Line 1 will compete against all other players in Line 1, and similarly, players in
additional lines will compete against all other players in their respective lines.
5.14.7. Every win earns one point, and overall points determine Gold, Silver, and Bronze
team winners. Ties are broken by regular season standings; the higher seed
wins.
5.14.8. All Championship Day games will be posted to DUPR but not recorded in the LMS.
5.14.9. Gold / 1st place division teams are named the Season’s Division Champions based
on Championship Day results, not regular-season standings alone.

4. DUPR RATINGS/DIVISIONS
4.1. Season DUPR Ratings: A player's Season DUPR Rating is established on the date
communicated to all captains prior to the first scheduled league match and remains in
eƯect for the duration of the season.
4.1.1. A player with a DUPR Reliability Factor below 29 will be classified as “Not Rated”
(NR) for League purposes and will be subject to the provisions of Rule 4.5. This
classification recognizes that a player’s current DUPR rating may not yet provide a
suƯiciently reliable indication of skill level, particularly for newer or less-established
players or those who have not recently recorded matches in DUPR. Players
classified as “NR” may be placed on a team in the division that most appropriately
reflects their current skill level while they record additional matches and establish a
more reliable DUPR rating. These players are strongly encouraged to consult with a
local Certified DUPR Coach, pickleball professional, or knowledgeable team
captain for guidance regarding appropriate division placement.
4.2. All DUPR ratings will be truncated to the nearest tenth to establish a player's “Season's
DUPR Rating”. For example, a rating of 3.496 will be truncated to 3.4, as will a rating of
3.401.
4.3. Some of our Leagues use the “Age-based” DUPR sub-rating but will still follow all DUPR
Rating/Division Rules. If a player hasn’t established their 65+ Age-based rating as of the
start of a season, their 50+ Age-based rating will be used.
4.4. Any player or team that is found to be cheating, tanking, game-fixing or any kind of data
manipulation, including intentionally creating multiple DUPR accounts, will be banned
from the League for one calendar year.

6.3. PrimeTime DUPR League
The PrimeTime DUPR League is exclusively for players age 65 and older who want
competitive play against others in the same age group. Using DUPR's 65+ age-based rating
system, the league provides a more level playing field by matching players of similar age and
ability. Separate men's and women's divisions compete weekly with two doubles teams
representing each squad, and any tied team match is decided by the exciting Picklebreaker
format. PrimeTime emphasizes spirited competition, sportsmanship, and the opportunity
for experienced players to continue enjoying high-quality league play in a community-
focused environment.

Viewing Your Play History
My Play History lets a player review their recorded league match results and performance
across the league.
Use the Play History Scope list to choose which results to view:
• All Seasons/All Teams
• A specific season, league, division, or team
The page updates immediately to show only results within the selected scope.
At the top, summary cards show:
• Games Played — the number of recorded match-line results in the selected scope.
• Wins — recorded individual line wins.
• Losses — recorded individual line losses.
• Other Category - Tracks non-counting personal games, such as forfeits and
Picklebreaker matches. Scores Pending — matches whose scores have not yet been
entered and posted.
Below the summary, each match shows the match date, teams, home/away status, season,
league, division, lines played, and available game scores. A match that still needs scoring is
clearly labeled Scores Not Entered rather than being shown as an unclear “Other” result.
Select More Player Details in the header to open a separate, scrollable details window. It
provides five additional groups of scope-specific information:
• Matches: wins, losses, and match win percentage.
• Games: individual game wins, losses, and game win percentage.
• Points: points earned, points against, and point differential percentage.
• Ratings: average recorded partner and opponent ratings, plus adjusted and overall
performance estimates.
• Last 5 Matchups: the player’s five most recent results, marked with W or L.
The details window is designed for mobile as well as desktop and can be closed without
changing the selected History Scope.
• Mobile Shortcut: Tap the Play History icon in the bottom navigation bar.

Rally Scoring Rules
We follow standard USA Pickleball rally scoring option rules (Section 14.A) with the
following clarifications/modifications:
• Service Positioning: After a side out, the first serve is determined by the team's
score: the player on the right (baseline facing the net) serves if the score is even, and
the player on the left serves if the score is odd.
• Switching Sides: Players only switch sides after winning a point on their own serve.
The same player continues serving from the new side.
• Side Outs & Scoring: If the serving team loses a rally, a side out occurs; the
opposing team earns a point and takes over the serve.
• Game Points: A team can win a point regardless of whether they are serving or
receiving except for the winning point (see next item).
• Scoring Freeze and Match Point: To keep the game competitive through the final
point, a scoring freeze shall take eƯect whenever a team reaches one point below
the game-winning score. Once a team reaches the freeze point, it may score the
game-winning point only while serving. For example, in a game played to 25 points,
a team’s score shall initially freeze at 24. The scoring freeze applies only to the team
that has reached the freeze point; the opposing team may continue to score using
normal Rally Scoring until it also reaches the applicable freeze point. A team must
be serving to score the game-winning point.
• Win-by-Two (2) Games: When the game is played using a win-by-two (2) format
and the score becomes tied at or beyond the initial freeze point, neither team can
win by scoring the next point. Therefore, both teams’ scores shall become
unfrozen, and normal Rally Scoring shall resume. Thereafter, a team’s score shall
freeze again whenever it reaches a score at which its next point would win the

17d347dd-9039-403d-b782-dae358725c0c.content:
PICKLEBREAKER™ GAME OVERVIEW
The Picklebreaker™ is our league’s tiebreaker format, similar to Major League Pickleball’s (MLP)
Dreambreaker. It is used when a match is tied after the day’s regular games. Unlike the MLP
version, our Picklebreaker uses doubles rather than singles.
Here is how it works:
The Format: The Picklebreaker™ is a doubles game played to either 15 or 25 points, depending
on the league. It always uses Rally Scoring, where every rally/serve earns a point regardless of
which team served. Refer to the league-specific rules for Rally Scoring, total points, and win-by
requirements.
The Rotations: Each team’s designated doubles pairs shall enter the game in the order
established by their captain prior to the start of play. Both doubles pairs currently on the
court shall remain in play until the combined game score reaches the next rotation
threshold, at which time both pairs shall rotate out and the next designated doubles pair from
each team shall enter.
For games played to 15 points, two (2) designated doubles pairs from each team shall
participate in the rotation, with substitutions occurring after every four (4) combined points
scored.
For games played to 25 points, six (6) designated doubles pairs from each team shall
participate in the rotation, with substitutions occurring after every four (4) combined points
scored.
Each newly substituted doubles pair shall resume play at the existing score and remain on the
court until the next applicable four (4) combined-point rotation threshold is reached.
If the game continues beyond the initial rotation of all designated doubles pairs, the
rotation shall return to the doubles pairs that began the game and continue in the same
