d3a82f34-48fe-41f7-8b51-69ca40f35d70.content:
Section 1 The Game
Pickleball is a paddle sport that combines elements of badminton, table
tennis, and tennis. It is played using a special perforated ball on a 20-foot
by 44-foot court with a tennis type net. The court is divided into right and
left service courts and a non-volley zone on each end of the net (Figure 3-1).
Pickleball can be played as singles or doubles.
In standard pickleball, the ball is served diagonally across the net to the
opposite service court on the opponent’s end, using an approved motion.
The ball is then hit back and forth across the net until a player fails to return
the ball in accordance with the rules.
Standard pickleball uses a scoring method where points are scored only
when the serving team wins the rally. The server alternates service courts
and continues to serve until they lose a rally (commit a fault). Typically, the
first player or team scoring 11 points and leading by at least a 2-point
margin wins the game.
Rally scoring has been provisionally approved as an option (Rule 14.A),
wherein a point is scored by the team that wins each rally. Mini-singles
(Rule 14.B) is a half-court variation of standard singles.
Unique Features
Two-Bounce Rule. After the serve, the receiver must allow the ball to
bounce before making their first return, and then the serving team must
allow the ball to bounce before making their first return.
Non-Volley Zone. The non-volley zone is the area of the court that
extends 7 feet from the net on each end of the court, within which a player
is not allowed to hit the ball out of the air before it bounces.
Wheelchair and Adaptive Play. Players using wheelchairs and players
having certain disabilities may allow the ball to bounce twice before
returning the ball. The first bounce must be in the court, but the second

0a229369-7a54-4ed9-bc9f-8de81b6bedaf.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
0a229369-7a54-4ed9-bc9f-8de81b6bedaf.heading: Scoring for Match Forfeit
0a229369-7a54-4ed9-bc9f-8de81b6bedaf.content:
22.K Scoring for Match Forfeit. When a match forfeit is imposed on a singles
player or doubles team, all their game scores are reported as zero (e.g., 11-
0, 11-0 for a two-of-three games to 11 points format; 11-0, 11-0, 11-0 for a
three-of-five games to 11 points format; 15-0 for a 15-point game format;
and 21-0 for a 21-point game format). Scores for matches completed
before the forfeited match are retained. (See Rule 15.B.4.a for a round
robin.)

21d16e11-80bb-4932-9624-6d324332b3b1.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
21d16e11-80bb-4932-9624-6d324332b3b1.heading: 23.B Withdrawal from Bracket — Scoring for Withdrawal
21d16e11-80bb-4932-9624-6d324332b3b1.content:
23.B.4 Scoring for Withdrawal. When a singles player or doubles team
withdraws from a bracket, the scores for each game of each
match not played are reported as 0-0. Scores for matches
completed before the request for withdrawal are retained. (See
Rule 15.B.4.a for a round robin.)

208b9c33-b755-4657-aa3a-45f6df0f277d.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
208b9c33-b755-4657-aa3a-45f6df0f277d.heading: Scoring for Game Forfeit
208b9c33-b755-4657-aa3a-45f6df0f277d.content:
22.H Scoring for Game Forfeit. When a game forfeit is imposed on a singles
player or doubles team, their score for the forfeited game must be
reported as zero (e.g., 11-0 for a game to 11 points, 15-0 for a game to 15
points, or 21-0 for a game to 21 points). Scores for games completed
before the forfeited game are retained. (See Rule 15.B.4.a for a round
robin.)

f411c1a3-01f6-4c90-830e-6f74d95cd81b.title: LWRPC-Captains Guide to the LMS
f411c1a3-01f6-4c90-830e-6f74d95cd81b.content:
Submitting Scores
Clicking Submit Scores saves the match results only when all player, team, and score
information is valid according to division rules. You cannot save any of the results (partial
save) if any information is invalid.
Once submitted:
• Notifications: The system automatically emails the opposing captains to notify
them that the scores have been entered.
• Verification: If your team is the first to enter the results, a captain of the opposing
team must log in to verify or dispute the scores to finalize the match and update the
league/division standings.
Score Verification Process
Use Pending Verification to review entered scores or raise disputes.
Selecting the appropriate button will:
• Finalize Results: Complete the scoring process for the match.
• Notify Captains: Automatically email all captains to confirm the match date and
scores are officially entered and locked.
• Update Standings: Instantly refresh the league/division standings.
Captain Dashboard / Pending Score Verification (red)

c83dd035-c4f8-440d-b504-7e1f5be14ace.title: LWRPC-Captains Guide to the LMS
c83dd035-c4f8-440d-b504-7e1f5be14ace.content:
Match Score Sheet
Once both teams complete Match Setup, print the Match Score Sheet to view match details,
player names, and the format of play. You are able to print this if both teams have not
completed their Match Setup but those teams not completed will be blank.
• Button Color: Stays red until both teams enter their lineups, turning green once
both setups are complete.
• Printing: Print the sheet only after the button turns green. Printing early will leave
missing lineups blank.
• Scoring: Use the printed sheet to record scores during the match, then enter the
final results into the system after all games are complete.
• Retention: Keep all completed physical sheets for the entire season in case the
league needs them for reference.
Email Opposing Captains
Click Email Opposing Captains to quickly message all captains on the opposing team.
Selecting this button opens your default email program and automatically populates the
match details, allowing you to type your message and send it directly.

b495d301-e3e4-4acb-abc9-842a05bb0eaf.content:

756ffd5a-ca1d-4905-b33d-825cab4d60a9.heading: 7.A Server Positioning — In Serving Area
756ffd5a-ca1d-4905-b33d-825cab4d60a9.content:
7.A.3 In Serving Area. Neither of the server’s feet is allowed to be in
contact with the playing surface outside the correct serving area

0d0682cf-e265-427c-b9f5-081fe825e4b0.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
0d0682cf-e265-427c-b9f5-081fe825e4b0.heading: Serve Placement
0d0682cf-e265-427c-b9f5-081fe825e4b0.content:
7.E Serve Placement. The server must serve to the service court diagonally
opposite their correct position. (See Rule 14.B.3 for mini-singles.) The served
ball must clear the opponent’s non-volley zone, with or without touching the
net, and land in the correct service court.

7028b4bf-5af0-47da-a004-0471881d5e6f.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
7028b4bf-5af0-47da-a004-0471881d5e6f.heading: 11.A Allowable Contact — Fault – Failure to Exit the Non-Volley Zone Before Volleying.
7028b4bf-5af0-47da-a004-0471881d5e6f.content:
11.A.3 Fault – Failure to Exit the Non-Volley Zone Before Volleying.
After contacting the non-volley zone, when a player volleys a ball
before both feet contact the playing surface completely outside
the non-volley zone, it is a fault against the player.

52c2308a-7527-427b-9e69-ebe5bbc93e0d.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
52c2308a-7527-427b-9e69-ebe5bbc93e0d.heading: 25.A.10 Volleying — Fault – Failure to Exit the Non-Volley Zone
52c2308a-7527-427b-9e69-ebe5bbc93e0d.content:
25.A.10.c Fault – Failure to Exit the Non-Volley Zone
Before Volleying. After contacting the non-volley
zone, when a player volleys a ball before both large
rear wheels of the player’s wheelchair contact the
playing surface completely outside the non-volley
zone, it is a fault against the player. (Modifies Rule
11.A.3)

906adaa3-1ff1-4fde-b868-e51d15b037bb.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
906adaa3-1ff1-4fde-b868-e51d15b037bb.heading: 11.A Allowable Contact — Fault – Non-Volley Zone Contact While Volleying
906adaa3-1ff1-4fde-b868-e51d15b037bb.content:
11.A.1 Fault – Non-Volley Zone Contact While Volleying. When a
volleying player or anything that has contact with the volleying
player (including the player’s partner) contacts the non-volley
zone, it is a fault against the player.

c855ae35-42d5-4797-b19e-46a48053caf3.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
c855ae35-42d5-4797-b19e-46a48053caf3.heading: Definitions

Imaginary Extension. The continuation of a line beyond its actual,
physical endpoint, as if the line were projected further even though it is not
drawn or present.
Line Call. An audible or visual signal that a ball in play has not landed in the
required court area.
Live Ball. The timeframe from the start of the score call until the ball becomes
dead.
Momentum. A property of a body in motion that causes a player to continue in
motion after contacting the ball. The act of volleying produces momentum that
ends when the player regains balance and control of their motion or stops moving
toward the non-volley zone.
Non-Volley Zone. The 7-foot by 20-foot area of the court on each end of the net
where players are not allowed to volley the ball. (See Rule 3.A.4.c for specifications.)
Officiating Team. Personnel under the leadership of the Tournament Head
Referee on or off the playing surface, including Lead and Second Referees, Tracking
Referee, Video Replay Referee, and Line Judges.
Paddle Grip Adjustments. Non-mechanical devices that change the size of the
grip or stabilize a player’s hand on the grip.
Paddle Head. The paddle, excluding the handle.
Permanent Object. Any object on, above, or near the court that can interfere
with play. Examples include, but are not limited to ceilings, walls, fencing, lighting
fixtures, net posts (including connected wheels, arms, and legs). Net cable or rope
on top of the net post, and other net support construction. Stands and seats for
spectators, the referee, line judges, spectators when in their recognized positions,
and all other objects around and above the court.
Plane of the Net. The vertical plane in line with the net extending above, below,

e87412ad-108c-41ca-ab5f-83fc1280d3ac.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
e87412ad-108c-41ca-ab5f-83fc1280d3ac.heading: 11.A Allowable Contact — Fault – Non-Volley Zone Momentum
e87412ad-108c-41ca-ab5f-83fc1280d3ac.content:
11.A.2 Fault – Non-Volley Zone Momentum. When a volleying player’s
momentum causes the player to contact anything (including the
player’s partner) that is in contact with the non-volley zone, even
after the ball becomes dead, it is a fault against the volleying
player.

38b54990-5601-486a-a582-5296295a2139.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
38b54990-5601-486a-a582-5296295a2139.heading: 9.B Faults — Calling Non-Volley Zone Faults and Service Foot Faults on

Opponent. Players may only call non-volley zone faults and service
foot faults on an opponent.

2753fb0b-c9a0-4e8d-bf70-5931b4ac4c01.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
2753fb0b-c9a0-4e8d-bf70-5931b4ac4c01.heading: 25.B.2 Assistive Devices — Fault – Non-Volley Zone Contact While Volleying.
2753fb0b-c9a0-4e8d-bf70-5931b4ac4c01.content:

When a player’s assistive device, or anything that has
contact with the volleying player (including the
player’s partner) contacts the non-volley zone, it is a

1e68b866-af7d-48b5-af0a-67043a4992ea.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook

a544ee56-f968-44ad-9695-71d0246fd2a4.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
a544ee56-f968-44ad-9695-71d0246fd2a4.heading: 7.E Serve Placement — Fault – Serve Lands in Non-Volley Zone
a544ee56-f968-44ad-9695-71d0246fd2a4.content:
7.E.2 Fault – Serve Lands in Non-Volley Zone. When a served ball lands
in the non-volley zone, it is a fault against the server.

d1bf63a0-79ce-48b9-bdd6-cb86c3e27333.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
d1bf63a0-79ce-48b9-bdd6-cb86c3e27333.heading: 25.A.10 Volleying — Fault – Non-Volley Zone Momentum
d1bf63a0-79ce-48b9-bdd6-cb86c3e27333.content:
25.A.10.b Fault – Non-Volley Zone Momentum. When a
volleying player’s momentum causes a large rear
wheel of the player’s wheelchair to contact
anything (including the player’s partner) that is in
contact with the non-volley zone, even after the
ball becomes dead, it is a fault against the

be178334-265a-4fb7-999e-9daf9ae40d17.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
be178334-265a-4fb7-999e-9daf9ae40d17.heading: 9.B Faults — No Enforcement of Other Faults
be178334-265a-4fb7-999e-9daf9ae40d17.section: Section 9: Dead Balls, Faults, and Hinders
be178334-265a-4fb7-999e-9daf9ae40d17.content:
9.B.4 No Enforcement of Other Faults. If a player believes an opponent
has committed any type of fault other than a non-volley zone fault
or a service foot fault, they may mention the specific fault to the
opponent upon completion of the rally, but they have no authority
to enforce the fault. The final decision on fault resolution belongs
to the player that allegedly committed the fault.

99125c66-9fbf-4552-90ba-b5f10e1f94b6.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
99125c66-9fbf-4552-90ba-b5f10e1f94b6.heading: 19.A Match Officiating Options — Referee Responsibilities: The referee is responsible for calling
99125c66-9fbf-4552-90ba-b5f10e1f94b6.content:

service foot faults, short serves, and non-volley zone faults.

81d39087-d987-4029-a3a3-83ea229e7f04.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
81d39087-d987-4029-a3a3-83ea229e7f04.heading: 9.B Faults — Fault Occurrence
81d39087-d987-4029-a3a3-83ea229e7f04.section: Section 9: Dead Balls, Faults, and Hinders
81d39087-d987-4029-a3a3-83ea229e7f04.content:
9.B.1 Fault Occurrence. A fault only occurs while the ball is live, except
for non-volley zone violations involving momentum. (See Rule
11.A.2.)

f7afa566-9c9c-4a48-9126-f1e84f5502f9.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
f7afa566-9c9c-4a48-9126-f1e84f5502f9.heading: Item on Court
f7afa566-9c9c-4a48-9126-f1e84f5502f9.content:
10.J Item on Court. When anything that is worn or carried by a player lands on
the player’s end of the court (except when the item contacts the non-volley
zone as a result of the player volleying the ball (see Rule 11.A.1)), the ball
remains in play, even if the ball hits the item.

d37a4a4b-e447-42e1-a00a-de1039617843.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
d37a4a4b-e447-42e1-a00a-de1039617843.heading: Definitions
d37a4a4b-e447-42e1-a00a-de1039617843.content:
and to both sides of the net.
Playing Surface. The court and the area surrounding the court designated for
playing.
Profanity. Words, phrases, or gestures commonly considered to be vulgar or
inappropriate in public or around children. Typically included are words used as
expletives or verbal intensifiers.
Rally. Continuous play that occurs after the serve is hit and before the ball
becomes dead.
Receiver. The player who returns the serve.
Replay. The restart of a rally without the awarding of a point or changing of the
server.
Retirement. A singles player or doubles team’s decision to discontinue playing in
a match in progress.
Second Serve (Doubles). A term used to describe the serving condition after the
first server loses their serve.
Second Server (Doubles). The first server’s partner. The second server serves
after the first server loses serve.
Serve. The initial strike of the ball with the paddle to start a rally.
Server. The player who initiates a rally by serving the ball.
Service Court. The area of the court on either side of the centerline, excluding the
non-volley zone. (See Rule 3.A.4.f for specifications.)
Serving Area. The area behind the baseline on each end of the court. (See Rule
3.A.4.g for specifications.)
Side Out. The awarding of the serve to the opposing team after a singles player or
doubles team loses its serve.
Starting Server (Doubles). For each doubles team, the player designated to
serve first at the start of a game.
Technical Foul. A one-point penalty assessed for extreme unsportsmanlike
actions or behaviors.
Technical Warning. A punitive warning assessed for minor unsportsmanlike
actions or behaviors.
Verbal Warning. A non-punitive caution for minor unsportsmanlike behavior,
usually given in advance of assessing a technical warning or technical foul for such

dcbf7ae4-2bfc-4204-93d5-e7acc382e6c8.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
dcbf7ae4-2bfc-4204-93d5-e7acc382e6c8.heading: “In” Ball
dcbf7ae4-2bfc-4204-93d5-e7acc382e6c8.content:
8.B “In” Ball. A served ball that clears the opponent’s non-volley zone line and
lands in the correct service court is “in.” A ball returned by a player that
lands on the opponent’s end of the court is “in.”

f5fc4515-e2d9-4939-9851-c5aaafcd887d.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
f5fc4515-e2d9-4939-9851-c5aaafcd887d.heading: “Out” Ball
f5fc4515-e2d9-4939-9851-c5aaafcd887d.content:
8.C “Out” Ball. A served ball that does not land in the correct service court on
the opponent’s end of the court, including one that lands on the non-volley
zone line, is “out.” Any other ball that lands outside the court is “out.”

ce40023e-98bd-42eb-bbc8-e18e6f9d18e5.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
ce40023e-98bd-42eb-bbc8-e18e6f9d18e5.heading: 20.E.2 Replays — Replay – Volley Serve, Questionable Ball Height.
ce40023e-98bd-42eb-bbc8-e18e6f9d18e5.content:
20.E.2.h Replay – Volley Serve, Questionable Ball Height.
When it is questionable whether the ball was no
higher than the server’s waist when the paddle
contacted the ball to make a volley serve, the referee
may call for a replay.

648d37fd-d84c-465d-9a40-c7b69948b37b.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
648d37fd-d84c-465d-9a40-c7b69948b37b.heading: 7.C Volley Serve — Fault – Illegal Volley Serve
648d37fd-d84c-465d-9a40-c7b69948b37b.content:
7.C.5 Fault – Illegal Volley Serve. When the server violates Rule 7.C.1,
7.C.2, or 7.C.3, it is a fault against the server.

798481f1-935a-4dc6-87d0-7c51994b8241.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
798481f1-935a-4dc6-87d0-7c51994b8241.heading: 20.E.2 Replays — Replay – Volley Serve, Questionable Paddle Head
798481f1-935a-4dc6-87d0-7c51994b8241.content:
20.E.2.g Replay – Volley Serve, Questionable Paddle Head
Height. When it is questionable whether the highest
point of the paddle head was no higher than the
server’s wrist joint when the paddle contacted the
ball to make a volley serve, the referee may call for a
replay.

9b929a1a-6aaa-489b-8e17-b09e9b48b00f.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
9b929a1a-6aaa-489b-8e17-b09e9b48b00f.heading: 17.D Officiating Play — Line Calls
9b929a1a-6aaa-489b-8e17-b09e9b48b00f.content:
17.D.10 Line Calls. Assist with line calls upon appeal and when a line
judge signals a blocked view. (See Section 19.)

74d16f9d-4708-4f41-8fb4-38ec8285c1e1.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
74d16f9d-4708-4f41-8fb4-38ec8285c1e1.heading: 17.D Officiating Play — Line Judges
74d16f9d-4708-4f41-8fb4-38ec8285c1e1.content:
17.D.12 Line Judges. Monitor and manage line judge performance. (See
Rule 20.K.)

d45024d9-24c6-4390-8a5b-4a0e9f0a7da8.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
d45024d9-24c6-4390-8a5b-4a0e9f0a7da8.heading: 19.C Matches with Line Judges — Invalid Line Calls
d45024d9-24c6-4390-8a5b-4a0e9f0a7da8.content:
19.C.3 Invalid Line Calls. Player line calls are not valid, except for their
centerline and to override an official’s line call to favor the
opponent.

90c71bf1-d6c4-477e-8458-df1824816c33.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
90c71bf1-d6c4-477e-8458-df1824816c33.heading: 17.C Pre-Match Briefing — Line Calling Duties
90c71bf1-d6c4-477e-8458-df1824816c33.content:
17.C.3 Line Calling Duties. Instruct players on the line calling duties of
the referee, players, and line judges when applicable. This
requirement may be satisfied by the Tournament Director
providing pre-match instructions to the players. (See Section 19.)

9c0b6869-c6de-415a-a2b9-ffdb96693a7a.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
9c0b6869-c6de-415a-a2b9-ffdb96693a7a.heading: 19.C Matches with Line Judges — Line Judge Responsibilities
9c0b6869-c6de-415a-a2b9-ffdb96693a7a.content:
19.C.1 Line Judge Responsibilities. Line judges make line calls and
foot fault calls for their assigned line and assist the referee with
other calls as requested. Line judges will signify by loudly calling
“out” (or “service foot fault”) and showing the “out” signal
(outstretched arm pointing in the out- of-bounds direction).

b06474ab-17e3-4c3b-a756-b087acd23347.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
b06474ab-17e3-4c3b-a756-b087acd23347.heading: 19.D Appeals — Loss of Opportunity to Make Line Call
b06474ab-17e3-4c3b-a756-b087acd23347.content:
19.D.3 Loss of Opportunity to Make Line Call. After appealing to the
referee or asking the opponent’s opinion on a line call, the
player and the player’s partner lose the opportunity to make the
line call, except to override the call to favor the opponent. (See
Rule 19.I.)

8177ef7b-31d6-4d8e-8538-890a8cf5c31b.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
8177ef7b-31d6-4d8e-8538-890a8cf5c31b.heading: Line Calling Responsibility
8177ef7b-31d6-4d8e-8538-890a8cf5c31b.content:
8.A Line Calling Responsibility. Players are responsible for making “out” calls
for all lines on their end of the court. In doubles, either or both partners may
make a line call.

2c4fae0b-1be9-4975-8695-32043828e9b6.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
2c4fae0b-1be9-4975-8695-32043828e9b6.heading: Player Override of Call
2c4fae0b-1be9-4975-8695-32043828e9b6.content:
19.I Player Override of Call. A player may override an official’s line call, their
partner’s line call, their own line call, or any “in” ruling when the override
favors the opponent.

c946676f-1fb0-4dfc-8ae5-a1072b518986.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
c946676f-1fb0-4dfc-8ae5-a1072b518986.heading: Line Judges
c946676f-1fb0-4dfc-8ae5-a1072b518986.content:
16.I Line Judges. The Tournament Director will determine which matches will
use line judges.

9011b1f6-3118-4d24-86ab-907a712a5265.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
9011b1f6-3118-4d24-86ab-907a712a5265.heading: Matches with Line Judges
9011b1f6-3118-4d24-86ab-907a712a5265.content:
19.C Matches with Line Judges. In matches officiated by a referee with line
judges:

9822e34d-b544-4a3c-820b-c4a720d90831.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
9822e34d-b544-4a3c-820b-c4a720d90831.heading: Matches Without Line Judges
9822e34d-b544-4a3c-820b-c4a720d90831.content:
19.B Matches Without Line Judges. In matches officiated by a referee without
line judges, players are responsible for making “out” calls for the baseline,
sidelines, and center service line on their end of the court.

37fed9dc-63ec-4bf2-8bfc-f59be4d2a52e.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
37fed9dc-63ec-4bf2-8bfc-f59be4d2a52e.heading: Partner Disagreement (Doubles)
37fed9dc-63ec-4bf2-8bfc-f59be4d2a52e.content:
8.H Partner Disagreement (Doubles). When partners disagree on a line call,
then conflict exists, and the team's call will be “in.”

29dc3955-725c-4131-ac89-7c8a8f1cda40.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
29dc3955-725c-4131-ac89-7c8a8f1cda40.heading: 22.B Verbal and Technical Warnings — Excessive Line Call Appeals
29dc3955-725c-4131-ac89-7c8a8f1cda40.content:
22.B.6 Excessive Line Call Appeals. Repeatedly appealing line calls in
a manner that disrupts the flow of play.

db3e475b-efd7-42a5-8a39-ff6475cf8715.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
db3e475b-efd7-42a5-8a39-ff6475cf8715.heading: 8.F “Out” Call and Signal — Valid Line Call
db3e475b-efd7-42a5-8a39-ff6475cf8715.content:
8.F.1 Valid Line Call. Any “out” call made by a player after the ball lands
is a line call.

a2e6e69f-ab8a-4469-a44b-d560b3f443e7.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
a2e6e69f-ab8a-4469-a44b-d560b3f443e7.heading: 20.E.2 Replays — Replay – Volley Serve, Questionable Upward
a2e6e69f-ab8a-4469-a44b-d560b3f443e7.content:
20.E.2.f Replay – Volley Serve, Questionable Upward
Service Motion. When it is questionable whether the
server’s arm was moving in an upward arc when the
paddle contacted the ball to make a volley serve, the
referee may call for a replay.

f5bbf238-3ff7-4777-905f-3eaf19a63a5c.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
f5bbf238-3ff7-4777-905f-3eaf19a63a5c.heading: Volley Serve
f5bbf238-3ff7-4777-905f-3eaf19a63a5c.content:
7.C Volley Serve. The service motion for a volley serve must comply with Rules
7.C.1 through 7.C.4.

b3767d2f-6e63-4e29-8e8e-c3910b8d4d44.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
b3767d2f-6e63-4e29-8e8e-c3910b8d4d44.heading: 20.E.1 Faults — Fault – Volley Serve and Drop Serve, Spin or
b3767d2f-6e63-4e29-8e8e-c3910b8d4d44.content:
20.E.1.e Fault – Volley Serve and Drop Serve, Spin or
Manipulation on Release. When the server
manipulates or spins the ball immediately prior to
the serve, it is a fault against the server.

bf196a1a-f6aa-4657-8fab-a9217e1b1685.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
bf196a1a-f6aa-4657-8fab-a9217e1b1685.heading: 20.E.1 Faults — Fault – Volley Serve, No Upward Service Motion.
bf196a1a-f6aa-4657-8fab-a9217e1b1685.content:
20.E.1.a Fault – Volley Serve, No Upward Service Motion.
When the server’s arm is not clearly moving in an
upward arc when the paddle contacts the ball, it is a
fault against the server.

22b23f1e-75e3-4ee5-9ada-e4bf509f6f8d.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
22b23f1e-75e3-4ee5-9ada-e4bf509f6f8d.heading: 20.E.1 Faults — Fault – Volley Serve, Paddle Head Above Wrist.
22b23f1e-75e3-4ee5-9ada-e4bf509f6f8d.content:
20.E.1.b Fault – Volley Serve, Paddle Head Above Wrist.
When the highest point of the paddle head is clearly
above the server’s wrist joint when the paddle
contacts the ball, it is a fault against the server.

00f6a270-657d-4c43-9ea7-fbd199cc4238.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
00f6a270-657d-4c43-9ea7-fbd199cc4238.heading: 20.E.1 Faults — Fault – Volley Serve, Ball Contacted Above Waist.
00f6a270-657d-4c43-9ea7-fbd199cc4238.content:
20.E.1.c Fault – Volley Serve, Ball Contacted Above Waist.
When the ball is clearly above the server’s waist
when the paddle contacts the ball, it is a fault against
the server.

aefe5998-e5fb-4198-bce1-f702d9cdd0f5.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
aefe5998-e5fb-4198-bce1-f702d9cdd0f5.heading: 20.E.1 Faults — Fault – Volley Serve and Drop Serve, Release from
aefe5998-e5fb-4198-bce1-f702d9cdd0f5.content:
20.E.1.d Fault – Volley Serve and Drop Serve, Release from
Hands and Paddle. When the server does not clearly
release the ball from only one hand or only from the
paddle immediately prior to the serve, it is a fault
against the server.

876b24ed-e6b2-4fa7-ba80-d5b99ae10b6a.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
876b24ed-e6b2-4fa7-ba80-d5b99ae10b6a.heading: 7.C Volley Serve — Forehand or Backhand
876b24ed-e6b2-4fa7-ba80-d5b99ae10b6a.content:
7.C.4 Forehand or Backhand. The serve can be made with a forehand or
backhand motion.

912eaf5c-704c-47c5-b41f-a49e4096920e.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
912eaf5c-704c-47c5-b41f-a49e4096920e.heading: 7.C Volley Serve — Ball Height
912eaf5c-704c-47c5-b41f-a49e4096920e.content:
7.C.3 Ball Height. The ball must clearly be no higher than the server’s
waist when the paddle contacts the ball.

c7ecfe25-6ffb-4132-9f02-b96d82c83125.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
c7ecfe25-6ffb-4132-9f02-b96d82c83125.heading: 7.C Volley Serve — Upward Arc
c7ecfe25-6ffb-4132-9f02-b96d82c83125.content:
7.C.1 Upward Arc. The server’s paddle must be moving in a clear
upward arc when the paddle contacts the ball.

a6cf0309-174e-4edf-8046-0e4460fcf480.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
a6cf0309-174e-4edf-8046-0e4460fcf480.heading: 9.B.3 Calling Non-Volley Zone Faults and Service Foot Faults on — Fault Call Timing
a6cf0309-174e-4edf-8046-0e4460fcf480.section: Section 9: Dead Balls, Faults, and Hinders
a6cf0309-174e-4edf-8046-0e4460fcf480.content:
9.B.3.a Fault Call Timing. A fault should be called as soon as the
claimed fault is committed or detected. The fault must be
called before the serve is hit to begin the next rally.

ed287040-6268-4cf3-9600-72cff8c92856.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
ed287040-6268-4cf3-9600-72cff8c92856.heading: 7.C Volley Serve — Paddle Head
ed287040-6268-4cf3-9600-72cff8c92856.content:
7.C.2 Paddle Head. The highest point of the paddle head must clearly
not be above the highest part of the server’s wrist joint when the
paddle contacts the ball.

aa72f7ab-1c39-40a5-9d25-ffa55513f881.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
aa72f7ab-1c39-40a5-9d25-ffa55513f881.heading: 9.B.3 Calling Non-Volley Zone Faults and Service Foot Faults on — Disagreement Between Teams
aa72f7ab-1c39-40a5-9d25-ffa55513f881.section: Section 9: Dead Balls, Faults, and Hinders
aa72f7ab-1c39-40a5-9d25-ffa55513f881.content:
9.B.3.b Disagreement Between Teams. When there is any
disagreement between teams about a fault call, the rally
must be replayed.

b7107119-e636-409f-ae5a-39bced5d7870.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
b7107119-e636-409f-ae5a-39bced5d7870.heading: 3.D.5 Prohibited Surface Features — Moving parts that can increase head momentum.
b7107119-e636-409f-ae5a-39bced5d7870.content: 3.D.5.e Moving parts that can increase head momentum.

1394dcef-5daa-4e48-a794-bf0aed6bf95c.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
1394dcef-5daa-4e48-a794-bf0aed6bf95c.heading: Catch or Carry
1394dcef-5daa-4e48-a794-bf0aed6bf95c.content:
12.C Catch or Carry. A player must not catch or carry a ball on their paddle
during a rally.

0382d619-2bde-46f6-a642-c003baef67b5.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
0382d619-2bde-46f6-a642-c003baef67b5.heading: 12.C Catch or Carry — Fault – Catch or Carry
0382d619-2bde-46f6-a642-c003baef67b5.content:
12.C.1 Fault – Catch or Carry. When a player catches or carries a ball on
their paddle during a rally, it is a fault against the player.

ae6c17b3-cb59-4222-b172-7e1a8de7df1c.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
ae6c17b3-cb59-4222-b172-7e1a8de7df1c.heading: 25.A.12 Tournament Events — Transition Between Standing and Sitting
ae6c17b3-cb59-4222-b172-7e1a8de7df1c.content:
25.A.12.a Transition Between Standing and Sitting. When
playing in a non-wheelchair event, a player is
permitted to transition between rallies from being
a standing player to a wheelchair player, or from a
wheelchair player to a standing player, but only
once per match. The transition will be treated as an
equipment timeout.

880f18b3-2e4a-42ce-b8b8-6eec2e369734.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
880f18b3-2e4a-42ce-b8b8-6eec2e369734.heading: 7.A Server Positioning — Grounded
880f18b3-2e4a-42ce-b8b8-6eec2e369734.content:
7.A.1 Grounded. At least one of the server’s feet must be in contact with
the correct serving area when the serve is hit.

09873d8f-8fdc-43f0-a8c4-ab83fd4c9907.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
09873d8f-8fdc-43f0-a8c4-ab83fd4c9907.heading: 25.A Wheelchair Play — Serving
09873d8f-8fdc-43f0-a8c4-ab83fd4c9907.content:
25.A.8 Serving. The moment the ball is served, both large rear wheels
must be on the playing surface behind the baseline and must not
touch anywhere outside the correct serving area. The front
(smaller) wheels are allowed to extend into the court when the
serve is hit.

36531db8-05fc-4dbe-b93d-386f91ca3952.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
36531db8-05fc-4dbe-b93d-386f91ca3952.heading: Definitions
36531db8-05fc-4dbe-b93d-386f91ca3952.content:
behavior.
Volley. A strike of the ball before the ball bounces.
Volley Serve. A serve made by hitting the released ball with the paddle before the
ball bounces on the playing surface.
Volleying, Act of. The act of volleying begins when the ball is hit out of the air
before bouncing (i.e., volleyed) and ends when the player’s movement from the
follow-through action (i.e., momentum) stops.
Withdrawal. A singles player’s or doubles team’s decision to be removed from all
upcoming play in a specified bracket.

3f776ea1-e2fd-4716-b123-4006bab07a10.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
3f776ea1-e2fd-4716-b123-4006bab07a10.heading: 20.E.2 Replays — Replay – Questionable Foot Contact Outside the
3f776ea1-e2fd-4716-b123-4006bab07a10.content:
20.E.2.e Replay – Questionable Foot Contact Outside the
Serving Area. When it is questionable whether either
of the server’s feet were in contact with the playing
surface outside the serving area when the paddle
contacted the ball, the referee may call for a replay.

50c1086b-0774-4f61-8eb8-795babd86cc3.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
50c1086b-0774-4f61-8eb8-795babd86cc3.heading: 20.E.2 Replays — Replay – Questionable Foot Contact with Serving
50c1086b-0774-4f61-8eb8-795babd86cc3.content:
20.E.2.d Replay – Questionable Foot Contact with Serving
Area. When it is questionable whether either of the
server’s feet were in contact with the serving area
when the paddle contacted the ball, the referee may
call for a replay.

71d35cd9-f8a5-49ee-ba56-e2471ded55f8.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
71d35cd9-f8a5-49ee-ba56-e2471ded55f8.heading: 5.A Singles — Server Position
71d35cd9-f8a5-49ee-ba56-e2471ded55f8.content:
5.A.1 Server Position. When the server’s score is zero or even, the serve
must be made from the right serving area and be received in the
opponent’s right service court. When the server’s score is odd, the
serve must be made from the left serving area and be received in
the opponent’s left service court. (See Rule 14.B.2 for mini-singles.)

ce177ab5-a288-43e8-a3b6-f6f7a1255804.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
ce177ab5-a288-43e8-a3b6-f6f7a1255804.heading: Replay – Player Repositioning
ce177ab5-a288-43e8-a3b6-f6f7a1255804.section: Section 6: Player Readiness and Calling the
ce177ab5-a288-43e8-a3b6-f6f7a1255804.content:
6.D.2 Replay – Player Repositioning. When the serving team changes
serving areas after the score has been called, the server must allow
all players to reposition, and then the score must be re-called to
restart the 10-second count.

4c5cfbe0-a9fe-4df3-9ec7-1c20e0f06a7e.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
4c5cfbe0-a9fe-4df3-9ec7-1c20e0f06a7e.heading: 13.I Player Crossing Plane of Net — After Hitting the Ball
4c5cfbe0-a9fe-4df3-9ec7-1c20e0f06a7e.section: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
4c5cfbe0-a9fe-4df3-9ec7-1c20e0f06a7e.content:
13.I.1 After Hitting the Ball. A player may cross the plane of the net
immediately after hitting the ball. The allowance to cross the plane
of the net only applies while executing the current strike of the ball
and for continuation associated with the current strike of the ball.

f0769772-76ed-4480-9f89-e58ce3acaf4e.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
f0769772-76ed-4480-9f89-e58ce3acaf4e.heading: 22.J Match Forfeit by Tournament Director — Improper Apparel

cecd431c-3051-409b-9e01-8ef7804f0975.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
cecd431c-3051-409b-9e01-8ef7804f0975.heading: Apparel
cecd431c-3051-409b-9e01-8ef7804f0975.content: 18.B Apparel. Player apparel must comply with Rules 18.B.1 and 18.B.2.

76911003-5ff6-44a3-93b5-61d245cb5b86.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
76911003-5ff6-44a3-93b5-61d245cb5b86.heading: 18.B Apparel — Apparel Change
76911003-5ff6-44a3-93b5-61d245cb5b86.content:
18.B.3 Apparel Change. A player must change apparel that is considered
inappropriate by the Tournament Director, including that which
approximates the color of the ball. A referee time-out will be used
for an apparel change required during a match. (See Rule 16.K.)

05daf200-c953-47d2-84af-f0e324cef372.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
05daf200-c953-47d2-84af-f0e324cef372.heading: 18.B Apparel — Depictions
05daf200-c953-47d2-84af-f0e324cef372.content:
18.B.1 Depictions. Graphics, insignias, pictures, and writing on apparel
must be in good taste.

9dd9fd0b-2292-4faf-ba7a-de8dfec69d4e.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
9dd9fd0b-2292-4faf-ba7a-de8dfec69d4e.heading: Equipment Time-Out
9dd9fd0b-2292-4faf-ba7a-de8dfec69d4e.content:
21.E Equipment Time-Out. Players are expected to keep all apparel and
equipment in playable condition.

3931d24b-23fd-44a3-9844-f99c675a73b8.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
3931d24b-23fd-44a3-9844-f99c675a73b8.heading: Player Apparel Changes
3931d24b-23fd-44a3-9844-f99c675a73b8.content:
16.K Player Apparel Changes. The Tournament Director has the authority to
require players to change apparel. (See Rule 18.B.3 and 18.B.4.)

577601f5-47a1-4ae1-a264-08fbd18ec5f4.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
577601f5-47a1-4ae1-a264-08fbd18ec5f4.heading: 18.B Apparel — Match Forfeit – Refusal to Change Apparel
577601f5-47a1-4ae1-a264-08fbd18ec5f4.content:
18.B.4 Match Forfeit – Refusal to Change Apparel. When a player refuses
to comply with the apparel rules, the Tournament Director may
impose a forfeit of the player’s match.

30afa7bb-5636-42cf-8fa7-b90f44a32d2a.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
30afa7bb-5636-42cf-8fa7-b90f44a32d2a.heading: Player Equipment or Apparel Problem
30afa7bb-5636-42cf-8fa7-b90f44a32d2a.content:
10.I Player Equipment or Apparel Problem. If a player experiences an
equipment or apparel problem during a rally, play must continue until the
end of the rally.

931e6361-cc91-4053-8d58-47d1e9294d22.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
931e6361-cc91-4053-8d58-47d1e9294d22.heading: 18.B Apparel — Footwear
931e6361-cc91-4053-8d58-47d1e9294d22.content:
18.B.2 Footwear. Shoes must have soles that do not mark or damage the
playing surface.

fd431edc-26aa-4d8f-bf8d-3217e9e2280f.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
fd431edc-26aa-4d8f-bf8d-3217e9e2280f.heading: Player Contacting Opponent or Opponent’s Court
fd431edc-26aa-4d8f-bf8d-3217e9e2280f.section: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
fd431edc-26aa-4d8f-bf8d-3217e9e2280f.content:
13.H Player Contacting Opponent or Opponent’s Court. A player or anything
that is worn or carried by the player must not contact their opponent or the
opponent’s end of the court while the ball is live.

cd0cf5b6-84a8-4744-a0f4-6972cb596a99.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
cd0cf5b6-84a8-4744-a0f4-6972cb596a99.heading: Starting Server Identification (Doubles)
cd0cf5b6-84a8-4744-a0f4-6972cb596a99.content:
18.C Starting Server Identification (Doubles). Starting servers must wear the
required form of identification determined by the Tournament Director. This
identification must be visible to the officiating team and players during play.

e24400e0-e8d2-48cc-a121-646c752f0d63.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
e24400e0-e8d2-48cc-a121-646c752f0d63.heading: 22.B Verbal and Technical Warnings — Objectionable Language
e24400e0-e8d2-48cc-a121-646c752f0d63.content:
22.B.1 Objectionable Language. Using objectionable language
directed at another person.

dea52fe0-dc3f-4d65-a360-baa86a427bbe.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
dea52fe0-dc3f-4d65-a360-baa86a427bbe.heading: Player Crossing Plane of Net
dea52fe0-dc3f-4d65-a360-baa86a427bbe.section: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
dea52fe0-dc3f-4d65-a360-baa86a427bbe.content:
13.I Player Crossing Plane of Net. A player or anything that is worn or carried by
the player must not cross the plane of the net when the ball is live, except as
provided for in Rules 13.I.1 and 13.I.2.

2cd4753d-dbb2-4127-8305-fe2dd6dc5811.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
2cd4753d-dbb2-4127-8305-fe2dd6dc5811.heading: Player Contacting Net or Net Support System
2cd4753d-dbb2-4127-8305-fe2dd6dc5811.section: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
2cd4753d-dbb2-4127-8305-fe2dd6dc5811.content:
13.G Player Contacting Net or Net Support System. A player or anything that is
worn or carried by the player must not contact the net or net support system
while the ball is live.

0da77239-2181-4785-ac98-173c0b7d8a30.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
0da77239-2181-4785-ac98-173c0b7d8a30.heading: Returned Ball Placement
0da77239-2181-4785-ac98-173c0b7d8a30.content:
10.C Returned Ball Placement. A player must return the ball so that the ball
lands on the opponent’s end of the court or contacts the opponent or
anything that is worn or carried by the opponent before the ball lands.

5928e2a6-501a-435f-a158-a1bdf4aec138.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
5928e2a6-501a-435f-a158-a1bdf4aec138.heading: 22.I Match Forfeit by Referee — Improper Contact
5928e2a6-501a-435f-a158-a1bdf4aec138.content:
22.I.6 Improper Contact. Making deliberately aggressive physical
contact with another person.

7641b385-17ab-4db4-9110-b4d8ad7312f9.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
7641b385-17ab-4db4-9110-b4d8ad7312f9.heading: 22.D Technical Fouls — Extreme Objectionable Language
7641b385-17ab-4db4-9110-b4d8ad7312f9.content:
22.D.3 Extreme Objectionable Language. Using extremely
objectionable language or profanity regardless of to whom or
what it is directed.

26932fd2-654a-4e73-a04e-186b171c3403.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
26932fd2-654a-4e73-a04e-186b171c3403.heading: 22.J Match Forfeit by Tournament Director — Improper Conduct
26932fd2-654a-4e73-a04e-186b171c3403.content: 22.J.2 Improper Conduct. Improper conduct between matches.

93760936-56b2-43de-bbb2-dd59310e3425.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
93760936-56b2-43de-bbb2-dd59310e3425.heading: 25.B.2 Assistive Devices — Part of Body
93760936-56b2-43de-bbb2-dd59310e3425.content:
25.B.2.a Part of Body. Assistive devices are considered part
of the player’s body.

65b11e66-561c-458f-a55f-83507210db8a.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
65b11e66-561c-458f-a55f-83507210db8a.heading: 3.C Ball Specifications — Color
65b11e66-561c-458f-a55f-83507210db8a.content:
3.C.3 Color. The ball must be one uniform color, except for identification
markings. Colors may vary.

ab0cae7d-473c-436e-9cd0-cf4848f5c142.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
ab0cae7d-473c-436e-9cd0-cf4848f5c142.heading: 22.L Ejection or Expulsion — Slurs
ab0cae7d-473c-436e-9cd0-cf4848f5c142.content: 22.L.1 Slurs. Using ethnic, religious, racial, or homophobic slurs.

93400f51-c155-4adf-ad8d-1fcb9e793a82.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
93400f51-c155-4adf-ad8d-1fcb9e793a82.heading: 3.D.5 Prohibited Surface Features — Anti-skid paint, paint textured with sand, rubber
93400f51-c155-4adf-ad8d-1fcb9e793a82.content:
3.D.5.f Anti-skid paint, paint textured with sand, rubber
particles, vinyl compounds, or any material that causes
additional spin.

9497ccb5-ed46-4f5b-9865-e9b73cb3c764.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
9497ccb5-ed46-4f5b-9865-e9b73cb3c764.heading: 22.B Verbal and Technical Warnings — Other Behavior
9497ccb5-ed46-4f5b-9865-e9b73cb3c764.content: 22.B.10 Other Behavior. Other minor unsportsmanlike behavior.

8f5bd3dc-8b0c-4852-925c-d4799b25f0e7.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
8f5bd3dc-8b0c-4852-925c-d4799b25f0e7.heading: 18.C Starting Server Identification (Doubles) — Match Forfeit – Refusal to Wear Identification
8f5bd3dc-8b0c-4852-925c-d4799b25f0e7.content:
18.C.1 Match Forfeit – Refusal to Wear Identification. When a player
refuses to wear the required form of identification, the
Tournament Director may impose a forfeit of the player’s match.

4f2f81d8-69ba-425f-ae26-f221b6ce7c07.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
4f2f81d8-69ba-425f-ae26-f221b6ce7c07.heading: 25.B.3 Two-Bounce Allowance — Player Identification Marker
4f2f81d8-69ba-425f-ae26-f221b6ce7c07.content:
25.B.3.e Player Identification Marker. At the Tournament
Director’s discretion, adaptive standing players using
the two-bounce allowance may be required to wear a
unique visible identification marker (e.g., a
wristband) during a match.

01b73714-fa01-4b03-8e75-b3c09ee5dda7.title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
01b73714-fa01-4b03-8e75-b3c09ee5dda7.heading: TEAM ORDER & ROTATION
01b73714-fa01-4b03-8e75-b3c09ee5dda7.content:
1. TEAM ORDER & ROTATION
1.1. Captains will create doubles teams from the current players and designate play order
including abiding by all DUPR team rating/division rules.

c43a2965-5150-423d-b010-50c2395c4b53.title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
c43a2965-5150-423d-b010-50c2395c4b53.heading: Weather Issues
c43a2965-5150-423d-b010-50c2395c4b53.content:
6.2.7. Weather Issues: If games are aƯected by weather-related issues and both teams
are unable to reschedule them within the permitted league timeframe, the
matches will officially be scored as a “weather related” resulting in a 13-13 tie.
6.2.8. Snacks/Drinks: Optional; the Home Team may provide them if desired.
6.2.9. Jamboree: held at the end of the season.

536619ca-b02e-454a-8fa3-d1f4cc8d8f94.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
536619ca-b02e-454a-8fa3-d1f4cc8d8f94.heading: 21.F Time-Out Between Games — Change of Starting Server
536619ca-b02e-454a-8fa3-d1f4cc8d8f94.content:
21.F.3 Change of Starting Server. Teams may change the starting
server between games and should notify the referee before the
start of the next game.

b59f7c08-67ed-4aeb-89ea-dfcd39aada69.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
b59f7c08-67ed-4aeb-89ea-dfcd39aada69.heading: 3.C Ball Specifications — Brand Identification
b59f7c08-67ed-4aeb-89ea-dfcd39aada69.content:
3.C.4 Brand Identification. The ball must have a manufacturer or
supplier name or logo printed or embossed on the surface.

e973c74e-c59f-40d4-a301-1e09eba7a4ea.title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
e973c74e-c59f-40d4-a301-1e09eba7a4ea.heading: CAPTAIN/CO-CAPTAINS
e973c74e-c59f-40d4-a301-1e09eba7a4ea.content:
2. CAPTAIN/CO-CAPTAINS
Each team in the League must be led by a designated Captain. That individual may also assume
the position of Co-Captain on a diƯerent team and can also serve as Captain for a team of the
opposite gender. However, an individual is not permitted to hold the role of Captain for more
than one team within the same gender category in a Division. A Captain or Co-Captain is not
required to be an active player on the team but may instead serve in a supportive capacity by
assisting with the responsibilities assigned to the Captain. For comprehensive “How to”
instructions for Captains, please consult the DUPR League Captains Guide.

bc275f0b-cf6e-4937-b0d9-d77e02f32ba5.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
bc275f0b-cf6e-4937-b0d9-d77e02f32ba5.heading: 20.K Removal of Line Judge — Player Request
bc275f0b-cf6e-4937-b0d9-d77e02f32ba5.content:
20.K.1 Player Request. When all players agree, they may petition the
referee to have a line judge removed.

7596c09a-5fc8-456d-8e39-64d3d40a99f6.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
7596c09a-5fc8-456d-8e39-64d3d40a99f6.heading: Electronic Equipment
7596c09a-5fc8-456d-8e39-64d3d40a99f6.content:
18.D Electronic Equipment. During competition play, players may not wear or
use headphones, earbuds, or any other equipment that enables audio
communication, except for prescribed or required hearing aids.

8797633b-8113-4aa8-bb92-4ba8cb6214b0.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
8797633b-8113-4aa8-bb92-4ba8cb6214b0.heading: Coaching
8797633b-8113-4aa8-bb92-4ba8cb6214b0.content:
20.G Coaching. Except during time-outs and between games, players or teams
must not receive coaching from anyone other than a partner.

af22a56a-e841-46b8-a89e-7c34b163fd52.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
af22a56a-e841-46b8-a89e-7c34b163fd52.heading: Ball Specifications
af22a56a-e841-46b8-a89e-7c34b163fd52.content:
3.C Ball Specifications. The requirements for the ball are set forth in Rules 3.C.1
through 3.C.5. The complete list of approved balls is posted on the USA
Pickleball website.

58f950f7-028e-4bef-bd1f-f873617aa3fa.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
58f950f7-028e-4bef-bd1f-f873617aa3fa.heading: USA Pickleball Approved Paddle
58f950f7-028e-4bef-bd1f-f873617aa3fa.content:
18.A USA Pickleball Approved Paddle. Players must use an approved paddle
that complies with the paddle specifications in Rule 3.D. Players must
confirm that their paddle is approved and listed on the USA Pickleball
Approved Paddle List.

f581de61-f30c-4350-91af-90fd116de4ea.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
f581de61-f30c-4350-91af-90fd116de4ea.heading: 3.C Ball Specifications — Design
f581de61-f30c-4350-91af-90fd116de4ea.content:
3.C.2 Design. The design of the ball must be approved by USA Pickleball
as detailed in the Equipment Standards Manual. USA Pickleball
Equipment Standards Manual

d8ceb05b-3e08-453a-88aa-26cb0b10a725.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
d8ceb05b-3e08-453a-88aa-26cb0b10a725.heading: Ball Selection
d8ceb05b-3e08-453a-88aa-26cb0b10a725.content:
16.G Ball Selection. The Tournament Director will choose the tournament ball
from the official list of approved balls posted on the USA Pickleball website.

409c67f0-3a33-4755-86ae-9fb80a170429.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
409c67f0-3a33-4755-86ae-9fb80a170429.heading: 18.A USA Pickleball Approved Paddle — Non-Compliant Paddle Discovered After Match Concludes
409c67f0-3a33-4755-86ae-9fb80a170429.content:
18.A.3 Non-Compliant Paddle Discovered After Match Concludes. After
a match has ended, when a player is discovered to have used a
paddle that is not listed on the USA Pickleball Approved Paddle List
or is not in compliance with the paddle specifications in Rule 3.D,
the match results stand.

11107397-c574-40c0-9570-2842773bddb4.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
11107397-c574-40c0-9570-2842773bddb4.heading: 18.A USA Pickleball Approved Paddle — Non-Compliant Paddle Discovered Before Match Starts
11107397-c574-40c0-9570-2842773bddb4.content:
18.A.1 Non-Compliant Paddle Discovered Before Match Starts. Before
a match starts, when a player is discovered using a paddle that is
not listed on the USA Pickleball Approved Paddle List or is not in
compliance with the paddle specifications in Rule 3.D, the player
must switch to a compliant paddle. There is no penalty to switch
paddles.

69847181-ecb4-48db-b617-47edac8da5c6.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
69847181-ecb4-48db-b617-47edac8da5c6.heading: 17.D Officiating Play — Damaged Balls
69847181-ecb4-48db-b617-47edac8da5c6.content:
17.D.14 Damaged Balls. Determine whether a ball is broken or cracked
and must be replaced, and whether the broken or cracked ball
affected the outcome of a rally. (See Rule 20.F.)

3bad457e-99c6-4967-9285-22782c3c3c10.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
3bad457e-99c6-4967-9285-22782c3c3c10.heading: No Definitive Call by Referee
3bad457e-99c6-4967-9285-22782c3c3c10.content:
19.G No Definitive Call by Referee. When the referee is unable to make a call
upon appeal, the outcome of the rally is determined by Rules 19.G.1
through 19.G.4.

b8e134cc-150c-47f3-8502-2e92e96b5000.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
b8e134cc-150c-47f3-8502-2e92e96b5000.heading: 19.C Matches with Line Judges — Player Responsibilities
b8e134cc-150c-47f3-8502-2e92e96b5000.content:
19.C.2 Player Responsibilities. Players are responsible for making
“out” calls for only the service court centerline on their end of
the court.

c5201d82-ecac-4191-af4b-cf6fbe85932c.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
c5201d82-ecac-4191-af4b-cf6fbe85932c.heading: Ball Release
c5201d82-ecac-4191-af4b-cf6fbe85932c.content:
7.B Ball Release. The server must comply with Rules 7.B.1 through 7.B.3 when
releasing the ball to make the serve.

56a317d6-c4b8-4e53-a4bc-e69139f5b357.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
56a317d6-c4b8-4e53-a4bc-e69139f5b357.heading: 20.K Removal of Line Judge — Referee Disagreement
56a317d6-c4b8-4e53-a4bc-e69139f5b357.content:
20.K.2 Referee Disagreement. When the referee disagrees with the
players’ request to remove a line judge, the referee must
summon the Tournament Director for a final decision.

826821d2-dafe-461d-b194-3ba70afc4b02.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
826821d2-dafe-461d-b194-3ba70afc4b02.heading: Local Rules and Exceptions
826821d2-dafe-461d-b194-3ba70afc4b02.content:
16.F Local Rules and Exceptions. The Tournament Director must not implement
or impose any rule that is not provided in this Rulebook. Exceptions to the
rules because of physical limitations of the courts or other local conditions
must be approved in advance of the tournament by the USA Pickleball
Managing Director of Officiating.

c214519f-9c2a-46c3-b70c-25e2be5f1408.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
c214519f-9c2a-46c3-b70c-25e2be5f1408.heading: Part III: (Sections 15 through 24) presents additional rules, and
c214519f-9c2a-46c3-b70c-25e2be5f1408.section: Part III: (Sections 15 through 24) presents additional rules, and
c214519f-9c2a-46c3-b70c-25e2be5f1408.content:
Part III (Sections 15 through 24) presents additional rules, and
modifications to rules in Part II, that apply to tournament play only.

cbafc499-9412-44c7-aa0a-858c6059d5e2.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
cbafc499-9412-44c7-aa0a-858c6059d5e2.heading: Notice of Matches
cbafc499-9412-44c7-aa0a-858c6059d5e2.content:
18.E Notice of Matches. It is the responsibility of each player to check the posted
schedules and notifications of schedule changes to determine the time and
place of each match.

23953127-f349-46c2-b1c9-f0c9365744c1.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
23953127-f349-46c2-b1c9-f0c9365744c1.heading: 22.J Match Forfeit by Tournament Director — Other Rules
23953127-f349-46c2-b1c9-f0c9365744c1.content:
22.J.5 Other Rules. Failure to comply with other tournament or facility
rules and procedures.

8c151056-67bd-49f9-8c62-7db683714ab7.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
8c151056-67bd-49f9-8c62-7db683714ab7.heading: 22.J Match Forfeit by Tournament Director — Venue Rules
8c151056-67bd-49f9-8c62-7db683714ab7.content:
22.J.1 Venue Rules. Failure to comply with the tournament or host
facility’s rules.

c2dda658-dc89-42b9-bff4-d94510c31d7a.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
c2dda658-dc89-42b9-bff4-d94510c31d7a.heading: 17.C Pre-Match Briefing — Rule Modifications and Hinders
c2dda658-dc89-42b9-bff4-d94510c31d7a.content:
17.C.2 Rule Modifications and Hinders. Point out approved rule
modifications, court abnormalities, and non-standard court
conditions that could be potential safety issues.

052926f8-eba7-4ed5-ae48-7f66d80da7eb.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
052926f8-eba7-4ed5-ae48-7f66d80da7eb.heading: Non-Officiated Tournament
052926f8-eba7-4ed5-ae48-7f66d80da7eb.content:
Section 24 Non-Officiated Tournament
Play
NOTE: In non-officiated tournament play, players administer their own matches
and report the results. All rules in Parts II and III apply to non-officiated tournament
play, except for those involving a referee or line judge, along with the modifications
set forth in this section.

5cd591a9-9b3b-4029-b96b-42c6c34464b1.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
5cd591a9-9b3b-4029-b96b-42c6c34464b1.heading: Scheduling Matches
5cd591a9-9b3b-4029-b96b-42c6c34464b1.content:
15.D Scheduling Matches. A player is not permitted to enter multiple events
scheduled on the same day with an overlapping time duration.

fc2a2336-2bc3-4fa4-9e3c-3455aeeb9ae5.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
fc2a2336-2bc3-4fa4-9e3c-3455aeeb9ae5.heading: 24.C Request for Referee or Tournament Director — Repeated Rule Violations
fc2a2336-2bc3-4fa4-9e3c-3455aeeb9ae5.content:
24.C.1 Repeated Rule Violations. The player believes that the
opponent is repeatedly violating one or more rules.

b7110c48-fa57-49ab-9e68-3119dc21bdf1.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
b7110c48-fa57-49ab-9e68-3119dc21bdf1.heading: 22.I Match Forfeit by Referee — Late Reporting for Multiple-Game Match
b7110c48-fa57-49ab-9e68-3119dc21bdf1.content: 22.I.4 Late Reporting for Multiple-Game Match. See Rule 18.F.2.

edf26617-2342-4ffa-9c84-b688e68312fa.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
edf26617-2342-4ffa-9c84-b688e68312fa.heading: 22.I Match Forfeit by Referee — Late Reporting for First Game
edf26617-2342-4ffa-9c84-b688e68312fa.content: 22.I.3 Late Reporting for First Game. See Rule 18.F.1.

2d2f67c0-55cc-4258-907b-110acc556f68.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
2d2f67c0-55cc-4258-907b-110acc556f68.heading: Mini-Singles
2d2f67c0-55cc-4258-907b-110acc556f68.content:
14.B Mini-Singles. All standard singles rules apply to mini-singles except for the
modifications included in this section.

c5792642-352c-49fa-a5c0-11399754fefe.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
c5792642-352c-49fa-a5c0-11399754fefe.heading: Notice of Schedule Changes
c5792642-352c-49fa-a5c0-11399754fefe.content:
16.L Notice of Schedule Changes. When any change is made to the tournament
schedule of matches after the initial posting, the Tournament Director must
notify the players of the changes.

3d90d00b-f874-40c8-8062-b0bbeaf553c9.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
3d90d00b-f874-40c8-8062-b0bbeaf553c9.heading: Code of Ethics for Line Calling
3d90d00b-f874-40c8-8062-b0bbeaf553c9.content:
8.D Code of Ethics for Line Calling. When making line calls, players must strive
for accuracy and operate under the principle that all questionable calls must
be resolved in favor of the opponent. The opponent gets the benefit of the
doubt on line calls made. Any ball that cannot be promptly called “out” must
be considered “in.”

421f169e-8581-4496-b26a-1eca2ef28f33.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
421f169e-8581-4496-b26a-1eca2ef28f33.heading: Removal of Line Judge
421f169e-8581-4496-b26a-1eca2ef28f33.content:
20.K Removal of Line Judge. The referee may remove and replace a line judge
for any reasonable cause based on the referee's own observation or the
unanimous request of the players.

689c988d-2899-42e1-bc35-13d53adc557d.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
689c988d-2899-42e1-bc35-13d53adc557d.heading: 19.G No Definitive Call by Referee — No Call by Players and Referee – Without Line Judges
689c988d-2899-42e1-bc35-13d53adc557d.content:
19.G.2 No Call by Players and Referee – Without Line Judges. Upon
appeal, when the players and the referee are unable to make a
call, the ball is ruled “in.”

5d4844de-9c0b-4c5f-80ce-e661af44957e.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
5d4844de-9c0b-4c5f-80ce-e661af44957e.heading: Removal of Referee or Line Judge
5d4844de-9c0b-4c5f-80ce-e661af44957e.content:
16.J Removal of Referee or Line Judge. The Tournament Director has the final
authority to remove and replace members of the officiating team. (See Rules
20.K and 20.L.)

43893efe-2e60-4de2-a511-cc2fdee8069e.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
43893efe-2e60-4de2-a511-cc2fdee8069e.heading: 19.G No Definitive Call by Referee — No Call by Referee – Without Line Judges
43893efe-2e60-4de2-a511-cc2fdee8069e.content:
19.G.1 No Call by Referee – Without Line Judges. When the referee is
unable to make a call upon appeal, the player’s call stands,
unless the player or the player’s partner asked the opponent and
the opponent made a definitive call, in which case the
opponent’s call stands. (See also Rule 19.D.2.)

df624c77-ee24-403f-9191-484b11fb1c87.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
df624c77-ee24-403f-9191-484b11fb1c87.heading: 19.G No Definitive Call by Referee — No Call by Referee – With Line Judges
df624c77-ee24-403f-9191-484b11fb1c87.content:
19.G.3 No Call by Referee – With Line Judges. When the referee is
unable to make a call upon appeal, the line judge’s call stands.

38a412dd-782b-41ea-8897-027688a74b85.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
38a412dd-782b-41ea-8897-027688a74b85.heading: Referee Makes Call – Without Line Judges
38a412dd-782b-41ea-8897-027688a74b85.content:
19.E Referee Makes Call – Without Line Judges. In a match without line
judges, when a player appeals a rally-ending shot to the referee, the
referee must make the call when they clearly saw where the ball landed.

940ff29d-d536-4d52-ba18-f99536774e64.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
940ff29d-d536-4d52-ba18-f99536774e64.heading: 8.F “Out” Call and Signal — Partner Communication
940ff29d-d536-4d52-ba18-f99536774e64.content:
8.F.4 Partner Communication. While the ball is in the air, any
communication between partners about whether a ball might land
out is considered player communication, not a line call.

a623493c-834e-4ded-8af6-ff3554c128b9.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
a623493c-834e-4ded-8af6-ff3554c128b9.heading: Match Officiating Options
a623493c-834e-4ded-8af6-ff3554c128b9.content:
19.A Match Officiating Options. Matches may be officiated by a referee with or
without line judges.

4e9e83b7-7473-4e8a-9368-5afb7a339528.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
4e9e83b7-7473-4e8a-9368-5afb7a339528.heading: Spectator Involvement
4e9e83b7-7473-4e8a-9368-5afb7a339528.content: 8.J Spectator Involvement. Spectators must not be consulted on any call.

6231971c-f7a2-4972-8943-ffb2e98111bf.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
6231971c-f7a2-4972-8943-ffb2e98111bf.heading: Referee Overrule of Line Call
6231971c-f7a2-4972-8943-ffb2e98111bf.content:
19.F Referee Overrule of Line Call. Upon appeal, the referee may overrule any
line call by a player or a line judge. The referee must overrule the line call if
the referee saw the ball land “in.”

fb919a5a-ae9f-4fcf-afa4-409e656a8ee1.title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR Captains Guide
fb919a5a-ae9f-4fcf-afa4-409e656a8ee1.heading: ENTER/VERIFY SCORES
fb919a5a-ae9f-4fcf-afa4-409e656a8ee1.content:
 Entering Match Scores: To enter scores, click the Enter Match Scores button in the
match. This option becomes available only on or after the scheduled match date and
will be red.
 Forfeits and Weather Delays: If an entire match date is forfeited or canceled due to
weather, notify League Management. They will log the information for that match and
update the standings.
 Score Entry Process: When entering scores, use the dropdown menus to select the
players for each game (built from your Match Setup), then enter the scores in each
game block. Click Submit when finished; the system will check for errors before saving.
 Score Verification: Once scores are submitted, the opposing captain will receive an
email request to verify them, and a red notification count will appear in their Pending
Match Verifications block. The opposing captain must open the match, review the
scores, and click the verification button (or dispute button if they don’t accept the
scores as written). Both captains will then be notified, and the standings will update
automatically.
o The visiting team captain must verify match scores promptly. This ensures there is enough time
to review the results and enter them into DUPR before the end of the weekend.

15165b05-cd31-4eb6-8bc3-2b0649075a16.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
15165b05-cd31-4eb6-8bc3-2b0649075a16.content:
USA Pickleball was organized to perpetuate the growth and
advancement of pickleball on a national level and to set goals
for worldwide play and recognition. USA Pickleball is committed
to furthering the growth and development of pickleball among
all players.
USA Pickleball published the sport’s first official rulebook in
March 1984.
USA Pickleball is the National Governing Body of American pickleball
that formulates and interprets all the rules of the sport in a manner
that preserves the traditional nature and character of the sport and
the skills traditionally required to play the sport. All such decisions
by USA Pickleball are final and cannot be appealed.
The purpose of the rulebook is to provide pickleball players with the
rules necessary for standard play (recreational, social, organized
league), and tournament play. Part I and Part II of this rulebook are
applicable to all play, both standard play and tournament play. Part
III modifies the standard play rules in Part II and is designed to be
used in the conduct of USA Pickleball sanctioned tournaments. Part
IV contains standard play and tournament play rules for players with
disabilities and modifies the rules in Part II and Part III. A sanctioned
tournament allows players to obtain a rating on a national or
international basis.
Non-sanctioned tournaments may also use these rules as guidelines.
Directors of non-sanctioned tournaments may be flexible in the use
of these guidelines to better fit the skills, ages, and diversity of their
players. It is recommended that non-sanctioned tournaments follow
this rulebook to prevent player confusion in future events. USA
Pickleball enthusiastically encourages these non-sanctioned
tournaments to promote knowledge and growth of the sport, as well
as skill development, while having fun playing pickleball.

4674abd2-5bad-42d6-9c6a-8d6ac976581d.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
4674abd2-5bad-42d6-9c6a-8d6ac976581d.heading: 25.B Adaptive Standing Play — Assistive Devices
4674abd2-5bad-42d6-9c6a-8d6ac976581d.content:
25.B.2 Assistive Devices. Players may use assistive devices such as
prosthetics, orthotics, braces, crutches, or canes during play.

0bbd1e05-0e7a-4614-8459-9c0216588dc9.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
0bbd1e05-0e7a-4614-8459-9c0216588dc9.heading: 25.A Wheelchair Play — Part of Body
0bbd1e05-0e7a-4614-8459-9c0216588dc9.content:
25.A.4 Part of Body. A player’s wheelchair is considered part of the
player’s body. The large rear wheels are treated like a standing
player’s legs for positioning.

290a29e9-a402-4f34-a5cf-38f85ba65e66.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
290a29e9-a402-4f34-a5cf-38f85ba65e66.heading: Adaptive Standing Play
290a29e9-a402-4f34-a5cf-38f85ba65e66.content:
25.B Adaptive Standing Play. Adaptive standing players must comply with
Rules 25.B.1 through 25.B.4.

3cc36e5c-defd-42b9-b029-1ca3970a5153.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
3cc36e5c-defd-42b9-b029-1ca3970a5153.heading: Paddle Specifications
3cc36e5c-defd-42b9-b029-1ca3970a5153.content:
3.D Paddle Specifications. The requirements for the paddle are set forth in
Rules 3.D.1 through 3.D.7. The complete list of approved paddles is posted
on the USA Pickleball Approved Paddle List.

f277df5b-1c8b-4239-9f8e-7fdf4fdb5829.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
f277df5b-1c8b-4239-9f8e-7fdf4fdb5829.heading: Paddle Compliance Appeal
f277df5b-1c8b-4239-9f8e-7fdf4fdb5829.content:
24.D Paddle Compliance Appeal. When any player believes a paddle is not
USA Pickleball approved or does not otherwise comply with all paddle
rules, the player may request that the Head Referee or Tournament
Director determine whether the paddle is approved.

0041e024-b5e1-4622-8149-5780841a1202.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
0041e024-b5e1-4622-8149-5780841a1202.heading: 3.D Paddle Specifications — Material
0041e024-b5e1-4622-8149-5780841a1202.content:
3.D.4 Material. The paddle must be made of material deemed safe and
not prohibited by these rules. Paddles must be made of rigid, non-
compressible material meeting the criteria specified in the USA
Pickleball Equipment Standards Manual.

96404043-0b73-4548-8c7c-a3b514a4a44f.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
96404043-0b73-4548-8c7c-a3b514a4a44f.heading: 3.D Paddle Specifications — Brand and Model Identification
96404043-0b73-4548-8c7c-a3b514a4a44f.content:
3.D.1 Brand and Model Identification. The manufacturer must have a
clearly marked brand and model name or model number on the
paddle and must also include the ‘USA Pickleball Approved’ seal or
text treatment. Paddles that were manufactured prior to the seal
or text treatment requirement must still be on the USA Pickleball
approved paddle list for sanctioned play.

4169a8b2-f10e-481b-b3c9-8b3d21cc2fa6.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
4169a8b2-f10e-481b-b3c9-8b3d21cc2fa6.heading: 7.B Ball Release — Release from Hand or Paddle
4169a8b2-f10e-481b-b3c9-8b3d21cc2fa6.content:
7.B.1 Release from Hand or Paddle. The server must release the ball
using only one hand or only the paddle.

65807c45-2fae-46b0-9ce5-cc6f16540f02.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
65807c45-2fae-46b0-9ce5-cc6f16540f02.heading: 22.I Match Forfeit by Referee — Dangerous Paddle or Ball Abuse
65807c45-2fae-46b0-9ce5-cc6f16540f02.content:
22.I.1 Dangerous Paddle or Ball Abuse. Aggressively or recklessly
striking or throwing a ball or paddle in frustration or anger that
strikes an individual or damages facility property.

1033d62e-3c9e-4103-9619-efa38398081a.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
1033d62e-3c9e-4103-9619-efa38398081a.heading: 22.L Ejection or Expulsion — Injurious Paddle or Ball Abuse
1033d62e-3c9e-4103-9619-efa38398081a.content:
22.L.2 Injurious Paddle or Ball Abuse. Damage to the venue or injury
to a player, official, or spectator through an act of paddle or ball
abuse or other acts of physical violence.

8e7073e9-0546-4ecb-b623-a6044f0852f0.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
8e7073e9-0546-4ecb-b623-a6044f0852f0.heading: 20.E.2 Replays — Replay – Drop Serve, Questionable Force on Ball.
8e7073e9-0546-4ecb-b623-a6044f0852f0.content:
20.E.2.i Replay – Drop Serve, Questionable Force on Ball.
When it is questionable whether the ball was
propelled when the server released the ball to make
a drop serve, the referee must call for a replay.

b38ff29a-208c-4ae4-a7c8-3b49f7ef6000.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
b38ff29a-208c-4ae4-a7c8-3b49f7ef6000.heading: 20.F Damaged Ball — Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball
b38ff29a-208c-4ae4-a7c8-3b49f7ef6000.content:
20.F.1 Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball. When the referee determines
that the broken or cracked ball affected the outcome of the rally,
the rally must be replayed with a replacement ball. (Modifies
Rule 10.G.1)

b72d7fc7-9099-4a74-9ddd-fbf864ec5a1c.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
b72d7fc7-9099-4a74-9ddd-fbf864ec5a1c.heading: 10.G Damaged Ball — Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball
b72d7fc7-9099-4a74-9ddd-fbf864ec5a1c.content:
10.G.1 Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball. When all players agree that a
broken or cracked ball affected the outcome of the rally, the rally
must be replayed. If all players do not agree that a broken or
cracked ball affected the outcome of the rally, the result of the rally
stands.

3135724a-c059-4e76-a0ee-b40240a596eb.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
3135724a-c059-4e76-a0ee-b40240a596eb.heading: 3.C Ball Specifications — Usage
3135724a-c059-4e76-a0ee-b40240a596eb.content:
3.C.1 Usage. All approved balls are acceptable for indoor or outdoor
play. (See Figure 3-2.)

c498fbdb-e47e-4da4-8544-f5b00352c321.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
c498fbdb-e47e-4da4-8544-f5b00352c321.heading: Net Specifications
c498fbdb-e47e-4da4-8544-f5b00352c321.content:
3.B Net Specifications. The requirements for the net and related elements are
set forth in Rules 3.B.1 through 3.B.7.

4fa8bc5d-0b85-420c-99cf-221c503b2eed.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
4fa8bc5d-0b85-420c-99cf-221c503b2eed.heading: 17.B Pre-Match Checks — Referee Tools
4fa8bc5d-0b85-420c-99cf-221c503b2eed.content:
17.B.1 Referee Tools. Check the availability and suitability of necessary
supplies for the match, such as balls, scoresheets, pencils, and a
timing device.

ac9b4567-2187-41ca-8618-026a5e37fe84.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
ac9b4567-2187-41ca-8618-026a5e37fe84.heading: Notification of Hazards and Abnormal Conditions
ac9b4567-2187-41ca-8618-026a5e37fe84.content:
16.E Notification of Hazards and Abnormal Conditions. Before the tournament,
the Tournament Director must notify players and referees of any unique
features, abnormal local conditions, or hazards associated with the courts.
When possible, players should be notified in writing as part of the pre-
tournament instructions. Referees must be notified at the venue.

f957817a-2df1-4652-aa2e-c8b4311e2378.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
f957817a-2df1-4652-aa2e-c8b4311e2378.heading: 15.A Event Categories. — Junior Events
f957817a-2df1-4652-aa2e-c8b4311e2378.content:
15.A.4 Junior Events. Junior events are qualified by ages 18 and younger.
Players aged 18 years and younger may play in any adult event
when a junior event is not available or does not have enough
entrants, or with the Tournament Director’s permission.

f9e44db6-6601-45c1-85d3-94883c746c58.title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
f9e44db6-6601-45c1-85d3-94883c746c58.heading: Forfeits
f9e44db6-6601-45c1-85d3-94883c746c58.content:
6.1.7. Forfeits: In the event of a forfeit (unable to reschedule and not weather related),
the match score is officially recorded as 7-0 in favor of the non-forfeiting team.

564f30d1-eab3-4c31-9035-d54b1fa60811.title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
564f30d1-eab3-4c31-9035-d54b1fa60811.heading: Forfeits
564f30d1-eab3-4c31-9035-d54b1fa60811.content:
6.1.9.5. Forfeits: In the event of a forfeit (unable to reschedule and not weather
related), the match score is officially recorded as 3-0 in favor of the non-
forfeiting team.
6.1.9.6. Weather Issues: If games are aƯected by weather-related issues and both
teams are unable to reschedule them within the permitted league timeframe,
the matches will officially be scored as a “weather related” resulting in a 2-2
tie.

82658134-49a3-4c6f-9e6a-ee8afd8acf0c.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
82658134-49a3-4c6f-9e6a-ee8afd8acf0c.heading: 25.A Wheelchair Play — Propelling Wheelchair with Foot
82658134-49a3-4c6f-9e6a-ee8afd8acf0c.content:
25.A.7 Propelling Wheelchair with Foot. A player who is unable to
propel their wheelchair with one or both upper extremities
(arms) for the entire duration of a match is permitted to propel
the wheelchair using a single foot against the ground. The player
is then subject to the following restrictions for the entire
duration of the match:
1) The player must not utilize their upper extremities for
propulsion.
2) The player’s foot must not be in contact with the ground
when the player strikes the ball to make a shot.
3) The player’s lower extremities must not contact any
wheelchair wheel.

7241fe46-7e1c-416d-9038-101eb48b99af.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
7241fe46-7e1c-416d-9038-101eb48b99af.heading: 25.A Wheelchair Play — Power Wheelchairs
7241fe46-7e1c-416d-9038-101eb48b99af.content:
25.A.3 Power Wheelchairs. Players unable to propel a manual
wheelchair for the duration of an entire match are permitted to
utilize wheelchairs powered by electric motors. Power
wheelchairs must be controlled by the player only and cannot
exceed 10 miles-per-hour.

6f6fdbce-6702-432d-a21c-6cb2dce834d6.title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
6f6fdbce-6702-432d-a21c-6cb2dce834d6.heading: 19.G No Definitive Call by Referee — Replay – No Call by Officiating Team
6f6fdbce-6702-432d-a21c-6cb2dce834d6.content:
19.G.4 Replay – No Call by Officiating Team. When the line judges and
referees are unable to make a call, the rally must be replayed.

cb5ef7b6-b312-4417-91a2-d55723e8af9b.title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
cb5ef7b6-b312-4417-91a2-d55723e8af9b.heading: Weather Issues
cb5ef7b6-b312-4417-91a2-d55723e8af9b.content:
6.3.8. Weather Issues: If games are aƯected by weather-related issues and both teams
are unable to reschedule them within the permitted league timeframe, the
matches will officially be scored as a “weather related” resulting in a 2-2 tie.
